picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech odds, spread and over/under for Week 9 Skip to main content SI.COM Wildcats in the Pros Brent Brennan and the No. 22 Arizona Wildcats have a crucial Week 9 game on deck, heading to Lubbock to take on the No. 13 Texas Tech Red Raiders on Halloween in a massive Big 12 showdown. A win would give Arizona a 4-1 record in Big 12 play, which would put them no worse than tied for second in the conference heading into Week 10 - and makes them a real dark horse contender for a spot in the College Football Playoff, or at least the Big 12 championship game. Arizona is 2-1 on the road this season, losing in Week 2 to BYU in Provo, but taking care of business against former Pac-12 foe Washington State in Pullman in Week 4 and dismantling West Virginia, 52-31, in Morgantown in Week 6. It has led to an excellent run game for the Red Raiders, who are led by J'Koby Williams and his 619 rushing yards and five touchdowns - good for a whopping 7.2 yards per carry. QB play hasn't been quite as consistent for coach Joey McGuire's club, with Will Hammond completing 67.8% of his passes for 1,561 yards - but only six passing touchdowns with six interceptions to boot. A monster Big 12 matchup hits Halloween as Arizona heads to Texas Tech for a game between two 6-1 squads that will inevitably shake up the standings. My Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction questions Will Hammond's quality, while my college football picks look at a 54.5-point total that might be too high. This game will be broadcast on ESPN at 12 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Arizona vs Texas Tech: Arizona +3.5 Play Arizona at anything +3 or above. Texas Tech has a quarterback problem. Will Hammond has 13 turnover-worthy passes to pair with only eight big-time throws (per PFF), and his limitations have resulted in the third least-explosive passing attack in the nation . That makes them one-dimensional offensively, and it plays into Arizona's run-stopping defense. The Red Raiders don't block well enough up front (118th in front seven havoc allowed) to compensate for the quarterback deficiency. Tech's secondary has been hit for 266.1 passing yards per game, so the Wildcats (10th in passing success rate) will be able to chuck it around. Arizona vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 54.5 Tech's offensive limitations will show through in this matchup. Arizona's defense (14th in EPA per play, 11th in success rate) is much better than the market is accounting for, as it doesn't have name recognition but is well-coordinated under Danny Gonzales. On the flip side, Tech's defense checks in at 16th in EPA per play allowed and 10th in PFF's team defense grade. The strength of this team still resides on that side of the ball, and Joey McGuire will attempt to lean on that unit and minimize possessions for Fifita. Arizona's top three wide receivers have all been out. Tre Spivey is done for the year, while Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter III are considered questionable. The Wildcats can still move the ball in the air, but the efficiency won't be at its peak given the cluster injuries. Arizona vs Texas Tech combo Arizona got off to slow starts against Washington State and Northern Illinois, and could do so again during a difficult trip to Lubbock. Texas Tech has cashed the First Half Under in eight of its last 13 games. Given Hammond's turnover-prone ways and overall offensive issues, the defense should be the focal point over the second half of the season. Under 27.5 in the First Half Arizona vs Texas Tech prop: First Quarter Under 10.5 Texas Tech has cashed the Under in the first quarter in 10 of its last 13 games. The offense could struggle out of the gates again, given Arizona's stingy defensive statistics. Arizona's offense has put up big numbers against lower competition, but doing so early on the road against an NIL-aided defense is a different ask. Pictured: Arizona Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita. Alex Hinton · Action Network Sat, October 31, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week was a very significant one for the Big 12 title race. Utah knocked off Houston as it hosted College Gameday. BYU could not avoid a letdown after beating Notre Dame as it lost at UCF in the Bounce House. However, many likely did not see Texas Tech losing at Cincinnati as a double-digit favorite. The Red Raiders fell to 3-1 in conference play and return home to face Arizona. Typically, Texas Tech, Utah, BYU, and Houston are the teams discussed when people bring up Big 12 Championship and College Football Playoff implications. However, Arizona is not to be slept on, as it is also 3-1 in the conference and sits at No. 22 in the AP Top 25. Arizona is alive and well in the Big 12 race and CFP with shots at Texas Tech and Utah in the next couple of weeks. If they are going to go on that kind of run, it will be led by senior quarterback Noah Fifita . That is where we will begin my Texas Tech vs. Arizona picks and college football parlay for college football Week 9 on Saturday, Oct. 31. Noah Fifita 250+ Alt Passing Yards (-130) Will Hammond 200+ Alt Passing Yards (+102) J'Koby Williams 60+ Alt Rushing Yards (-154) Parlay Odds: +448 ( FanDuel ) Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds As a four-year starter, Noah Fifita has thrown for over 11,000 passing yards and only needs nine touchdowns to reach 100 for his career. However, his senior season is on track to be the best one of his career. Fifita heads into Lubbock this week, completing 74.2% of his passes while throwing for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He ranks in the top 20 among FBS quarterbacks in passing yards, touchdown passes and QBR. Fifita is averaging 292.4 passing yards per game this season. He has thrown for 250 yards in six of his first seven games this season and eight of his last nine dating back to last season. He has only faced Texas Tech once in his career, and while he did throw two interceptions, he also threw for 301 yards on 49 attempts. He is coming off consecutive 300-yard games, and a third may be in the cards this week. The Red Raiders are allowing 266.1 passing yards per game, and they have allowed 275 passing yards in four of their past six games. They also rank 86th in passing Success Rate allowed and 106th in explosiveness allowed. Averaging 9.2 yards per attempt this season, Fifita should take advantage. Lost in the Brendan Sorsby saga was the fact that Texas Tech had another starting-caliber quarterback on the roster. Will Hammond was just recovering from a torn ACL. After flashing in spot duty, Hammond has underwhelmed to a degree this season. He has six touchdowns and six interceptions on the year and ranks 51st in QBR. However, he has also thrown for 1,561 yards and is averaging 223 yards per game. Hammond has thrown for 200 yards in five of his seven starts this season, including each of the Red Raiders' four home games. He's averaging 253 passing yards per game at home this season and faces a Wildcats defense that allows 207.7 passing yards per game. It will help Hammond this week having both of his standout running backs available. Cameron Dickey was injured in the victory over Colorado and has missed the Red Raiders' last two games. J'Koby Williams picked up the slack, rushing for 165 yards against Arizona State and 81 at Cincinnati last week. He leads the team with 619 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 7.2 yards per carry. However, even when Dickey has been available, Williams has run for at least 60 yards in four of his five games and six of his seven overall. He will face an Arizona defense that has been strong against the run, ranking 10th in Rushing Success Rate allowed. It's allowing 107.7 rushing yards per game and 3.1 yards per carry. However, the Wildcats are 126th in explosiveness allowed. That should benefit both Hammond and particularly Williams, who has had a 20-yard rush in each of his last six games.

picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction: One fatal flaw that could decide everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction: One fatal flaw that could decide everything Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A critical Big 12 matchup tees off in this weekend's college football action as Arizona and Texas Tech meet in a matchup of AP top 25 ranked rivals. Both have one loss and sit in a tie for second place in the competitive Big 12 standings. Texas Tech just took a surprise loss at Cincinnati and Arizona is on an impressive five-game win streak. Whoever loses this one could see their College Football Playoff ambitions vanish into thin air. Who has the ultimate advantage? How Arizona can win Sep 5, 2026; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Arizona Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita (1) celebrates a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images Arizona has the passing-game firepower to make this a competitive matchup, but the Wildcats need to turn that strength into sustained offensive production. Noah Fifita leads an offense averaging 310.9 passing yards per game, ninth-best nationally. And this offense is third in FBS converting almost 55 percent of its third downs. Texas Tech is third-worst in the Big 12 against the pass and second-worst with 16 touchdowns allowed. Those numbers suggest the Wildcats can move the chains against this defense. The key remains protecting Fifita, establishing a running game to keep the Tech defense honest, and critically avoiding turnovers. Defensively, Arizona also needs to continue its recent success against the run. It held Iowa State to just 52 rushing yards in a 39-3 victory last week. Controlling the ground game forces the Red Raiders to throw the ball, something they're not doing all that consistently. MORE: Week 9 college football upset watch: Arizona, Clemson top road threats How Texas Tech can win Sep 26, 2026; Lubbock, Texas, USA; Texas Tech Red Raiders running back Cameron Dickey (8) rushes against Sam Houston Bearkat defensive tackle Justin Terrell (98) in the second half at Galaxy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Balancing out this offense is crucial for the Red Raiders. Surprisingly, they rank in the bad half of the Big 12 in total offensive and defensive efficiency. The good news is they can run the ball moderately well, averaging 190 yards per game and 5 yards per carry. Running effectively helps Texas Tech control the tempo, keep Noah Fifita and Arizona's potent passing attack on the sideline, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Will Hammond. Texas Tech needs to consider giving backup quarterback Tommy Castellanos more opportunities. Hammond has struggled – 6 TDs, 6 INTs – while the guy behind him on the depth chart introduces a kind of mobility that is harder to defend. More: 4 bold college football predictions for Week 9 games from The Big Lead The key matchup The one potential fatal flaw Texas Tech could expose this weekend is Arizona's vulnerability to interior pass pressure. That's an area where the Red Raiders' pass rush is still pretty good. Arizona has allowed 17 sacks this season, ranking third-worst in the Big 12. Tech's interior pass rush could force Fifita to move off his spot and make decisions before his receivers finish their routes. If Texas Tech generates pressure without blitzing heavily, it can keep extra defenders in coverage and make Arizona work much harder for completions. More: Predicting Big 12 football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Arizona is averaging 311 passing yards per game, while the Red Raiders are allowing 266. That's a significant opportunity for Fifita to expose a defense that showed real structural vulnerability in the loss to Cincinnati. The Wildcats also have better defensive numbers, allowing just 16 points per game. The Red Raiders can run the ball well at home, but Arizona's passing efficiency and defensive consistency give it a path to a very real upset. The Big Lead prediction: Arizona 30, Texas Tech 27

Score prediction for Arizona game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Things have taken quite the turn for the Texas Tech football team after suffering its first loss of the season. Getting bested by Cincinnati for 60 minutes has put the Red Raiders in a pressure point. There's little wiggle room left for Joey McGuire's team to keep its hopes of repeating as Big 12 Conference champions alive. Now they have a talented Arizona team coming to Galaxy Stadium looking to kick the Red Raiders while they're down. What will it take for Texas Tech to walk away with the win? Is Arizona actually the favorite in this game? Our breakdown of the game, plus a score prediction. What's holding Texas Tech football back? It's a layered conversation as to what is keeping the Red Raiders from reaching their potential. For starters, the offense, led by quarterback Will Hammond, hasn't put up the kind of numbers Tech fans want. Receivers have struggled to get open (besides Kenny Johnson) and when they do create separation from their defenders, Hammond hasn't found them or delivered solid throws enough to take advantage. While the rushing game has been a point of scorn for some fans, J'Koby Williams has been electric, and Cameron Dickey is on track to rejoin him in the backfield this week. Defensively, the pass defense has been sporadic. The 13 interceptions (second in the nation) and five pick-6s count, but when those haven't come, opponents have had little trouble moving the ball through the air against the Red Raiders. These things have been present all year but only came to a head against Cincinnati. Now they face an Arizona team equipped to exploit these very issues. TEMPE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 25: Quarterback Noah Fifita #11 of the Arizona Wildcats walks out to the field before the NCAAF game against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Mountain America Stadium on November 25, 2023 in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) What Arizona football can do to beat Texas Tech football The Wildcats rank sixth in the nation in total sacks (24.0), bringing constant pressure to opposing quarterbacks to get them out of rhythm. Cincinnati generated a season-high four sacks against the Red Raiders last week, while Arizona has three games with five or more sacks. Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have also been operating at a high level, generating at least 280 yards through the air in six of the team's seven games. Fifita ranks third in the Big 12 with 2,064 passing yards, totaling 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions. The Wildcats have been hit with injuries to their receiving room, having already lost Tre Spivey for the season and seeing two others on the team's first availability report for the game. Even so, Arizona's offense has operated at a high level. Texas Tech football's notable streak on the line The Red Raiders have won their last 12 home games, which ranks one shy of the program record set during World War II when the Red Raiders won 13 straight games from 1939 to 1942. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs. Arizona Arizona 35, Texas Tech 21: This is a pivot point for the Red Raiders to determine where they'll be in the Big 12 title race. Problem is, Texas Tech struggled to generate offense against a bad Cincinnati defense, and Arizona's defense has been quality all season. Bad recipe. picks.blurb: Life comes at you fast. BYU and Texas Tech are licking their wounds after road losses to unranked teams and the league's commissioner Brett Yormark is headed out the door . The Red Raiders ' loss at Cincinnati stirred up a hornet's nest after Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell took to social media , saying: "There is no excuse or reason to lose a game like this. We have to be better." He stayed on social media throughout the week, dispelling any notion Tech coach Joey McGuire was under any sort of heat : "Joey McGuire is a perfect fit for our program, everybody, with an opinion that matters, loves him. He isn’t going anywhere." While the Red Raiders were feeling the burn of defeat, Wildcats fans were enjoying the burn of tequila. Arizona coach Brent Brennan ran up a $2,000 bar tab buying tequila shots for fans after the Wildcats' 39-3 homecoming win over Iowa State last Saturday. "I think it's important that if you want people to show up for you, you've got to show up for them and it was just an easy way for me to pop in there with all of our alumni in town and everybody for Homecoming and the excitement of the game to just go in there and say hello and get out," Brennan said. "I was there for five minutes and it was an expensive five minutes, but it was good five minutes." Just trying to invest in our fans and just let them know how much we appreciate them as a football team." Texas Tech (6-1, 3-1) fell from No. 5 in the US LBM Coaches poll to No. 14, while the Wildcats (6-1, 3-1) enter the Coaches Poll at No. 21 after five straight wins. Saturday's game has the potential to be a Big 12 championship game eliminator. So who wins? Here's what you need to know for one of Week 9's marquee games , including predictions from USA TODAY Sports reporters and beat writers from the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal , Arizona Republic and Arizona Daily Star , part of the USA TODAY Network. We’re going to go with the guy who’s simply playing better football this season." — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY Arizona 35, Texas Tech 21: This is a pivot point for the Red Raiders to determine where they'll be in the Big 12 title race. away.headline: R.J. Mosley injury updates: Arizona WR suffers scary injury vs Texas Tech
away.blurb: After the play, Mosley reached for his left knee and remained on the turf, with team medical personnel rushing out to tend to him. As Mosley stayed down, Wildcats coaches and players began gathering around him while the crowd at Texas Tech's Galaxy Stadium fell silent. R.J. Mosley, a wide receiver for No. 21 Arizona , had to be carted off the field of his team's game against No. 14 Texas Tech late in the third quarter after suffering a knee injury on an eight-yard reception. The ESPN broadcast of the game noted that the decision was made not to show replays of the injury, speaking to its severity or visually gruesome nature. The injury occurred with the Wildcats trailing the Red Raiders , 24-23, with 1:27 remaining in the second quarter in a game with significant Big 12 championship implications. Here's the latest on Mosley's injury: With his team trailing Texas Tech by one late in the third quarter, Mosley caught a short pass from quarterback Noah Fifita on third-and-18 for an eight-yard completion to the Arizona 25-yard line, where he was met with a hard hit by Red Raiders cornerback Amier Boyd. On the ESPN broadcast, play-by-play man Dave Pasch noted that the network's production truck opted not to show a replay of the reception and the tackle that resulted in the injury. After several minutes, Mosley was placed on a cart and driven off the field. Early in the fourth quarter, ESPN sideline reporter Taylor McGregor said that Mosley was undergoing x-rays on his lower body to determine the nature and severity of the injury. He was later transported to an area hospital for further evaluation and treatment. A freshman from Brentwood, California, Mosley has seven catches for 107 yards this season. After the game, Arizona coach Brent Brennan said he didn't have any updates on Mosley, though he was thankful to Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire, saying, "they've been very, very helpful with that process."

picks.headline: Iowa vs. Wisconsin Prediction: Hawkeye Halloween Horror, But For Who?
picks.blurb: Iowa vs. Wisconsin Prediction: Hawkeye Halloween Horror, But For Who? Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS It's the Big Ten. There's no time to sulk over losses or complain about things not working out. Another week presents another tough test and an opportunity to right the ship. The Iowa Hawkeyes are back in action against the Wisconsin Badgers for the Battle of the Heartland, so let's dig in. Iowa lost its last outing to Minnesota in one of the sloppiest games the Hawkeyes have played under Kirk Ferentz in years. Wisconsin, on the other hand, comes to Kinnick Stadium fresh off a very strong showing in a win against USC. Iowa vs Wisconsin betting odds, spread, total Spread: Iowa -3.5 (-105), Wisconsin +3.5 (-115) Money Line: Iowa -170, Wisconsin +142 Total: Over 36.5 (-112), Under 36.5 (-108) Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Iowa opened as 4.5-point favorites, so there has been some slight movement toward Wisconsin, but nothing drastic in the overall feel of Iowa being the home favorite this week. The same can't be said for the total. The total has dropped three points to 36.5, a number fitting for this matchup. How to watch Iowa vs Wisconsin, time, TV channel, streaming Time: 11 a.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa TV Channel: FS1 Streaming: FOX Sports App Iowa is getting the primetime coverage from FOX on this one. The Hawkeyes and Badgers get the FOX Big Noon Kickoff, which means all of the pomp and circumstance is coming to Iowa City. Expect Kinnick Stadium to be charged up for this Big Ten rivalry. Riley Donald's Iowa vs Wisconsin Prediction Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13 I have no reason to believe we are going to see offensive fireworks in this game. Iowa knows the advantage its defense has over Wisconsin's offense and vice versa. These offenses are going to come out cautiously, not looking to make the big turnover that puts them behind. It's a classic Iowa game, really. Iowa is going to turn this to its defense, let the punt unit do its job of pinning Wisconsin deep, and find just enough juice via one or two big plays or short fields set up by winning the turnover battle. More than anything, Iowa is simply elite after a loss under Kirk Ferentz. This game has all the makings of an inspired performance from the Hawkeyes after doing everything wrong last week. Iowa gets back on track with a gritty, old-school Big Ten rivalry win. Iowa uses all of its usual tricks of suffocating the offense, doing the little things right, and making life hard on Wisconsin. It's Iowa's Halloween tricks that are scary no matter how many times it's done. Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS While the Floyd of Rosedale slipped out of the Iowa Hawkeyes ' grasp, another trophy is on the line this week when the Wisconsin Badgers come to Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The Battle for the Heartland trophy is going to be up for grabs. Iowa has dominated the Badgers for the last two seasons in two blowout wins, but this year looks like it will be a different type of game. These teams mirror each other quite well. Both play good defense, want to run the ball, and are winning games. It figures to be a four-quarter battle in this rivalry. Iowa holds Wisconsin under 150 yards passing This is a day when Iowa's secondary can shine, as we have seen in so many previous seasons. The group looks strong, led by Zach Lutmer. Outside, Jaylen Watson and Deshaun Lee are playing at a really high level, while Xavier Styles is growing each week at safety. Phil Parker is going to have Iowa containing Colton Joseph in the pocket, forcing him to beat Iowa with his arm. If Iowa can corral him and make him make tight-window throws all game, it's going to be a long day of incompletions and potentially some turnovers. DJ Vonnahme leads Iowa's passing game My gut tells me that Iowa's offense is going to have a very "2024" feel to it, like it did with Kaleb Johnson and all of the under-center zone runs. This is where DJ Vonnahme can feast. He can be the easy, big target for Hank Brown off of heavy play-action when the defense starts to flow. Iowa should look to Vonnahme early and often to get him the ball and set him up to run after the catch. When found in passing situations, I really like DJ Vonnahme down the seam. He can run and carry this route, plus he has the feel to find green grass between the linebackers and safeties. Iowa averages more yards per rush than Wisconsin Hear me out for one second - neither run game is going to be overly pretty in this game. Just prepare yourselves for that. These defenses are going to commit so many resources to stopping the run that even if responsibilities are messed up, there will be backup on standby to clean up the mess. I think Iowa's defense is going to eliminate much of the success for Wisconsin by containing Colton Joseph, which is a specialty of Phil Parker, and therefore force the backs to make something happen. Iowa can stop the run in its base defense, which it should be in for most of this game. Offensively, it won't be pretty for Iowa, but I think the Hawkeyes have a spirited run game that converts some ugly short-yardage plays and stays patient enough to get a few chunks from the running back room. It will take time, but Iowa's run game gets going just enough in this one. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Culture-Defining Clash With Iowa on Halloween Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL How big is the Badgers game this weekend? They're playing Iowa . Enough said. Forget the Big Ten race and the postseason implications. Forget the fact that Wisconsin has a chance to build on a tremendous win over then-No. 16 USC last week. Even forget the fact that the Badgers have lost four straight in this series. When Wisconsin plays Iowa, it's a battle between two like-minded programs. Two teams that want nothing more than to impose their will on opponents via a punishing ground game and stout, tenacious defense. This is the game, year in and year out, that provides the litmus test for the Badgers. Just how physical, how tough are they? How badly do they want it? As we continue to preview the enormous showdown in Iowa City, I've got three bold predictions for the Big Noon Kickoff clash: Colton Joseph bounces back Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Iowa has an extremely intimidating defense, especially when you have to play them on the road. Defensive coordinator Phil Parker, as he always does, has that unit playing at an elite level. The Hawkeyes rank No. 14 in total defense, including No. 5 in run defense allowing just 82.9 yards per game on the ground. Iowa has an extremely intimidating defense, especially when you have to play them on the road. Defensive coordinator Phil Parker, as he always does, has that unit playing at an elite level. The Hawkeyes rank No. 14 in total defense, including No. 5 in run defense allowing just 82.9 yards per game on the ground. However, their pass defense has been a little shakier. They rank No. 48 nationally, allowing 198.4 yards per game. Across Big Ten play, the secondary has been less reliable; through four conference games, the Hawkeyes allow 264.3 passing yards per game. That includes letting now-benched Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood toss for 276 yards, and allowing Washington's backup quarterback Elijah Brown to toss for 251 of the 320 total passing yards they surrendered to the Huskies. Iowa's outside cornerbacks have posted some impressive numbers. Jaylen Watson and Deshaun Lee boast reception percentages allowed of 46.9 and 54.2, respectively, while the latter has three interceptions. Still, I see Colton Joseph and Wisconsin's passing game bouncing back a bit Saturday in Iowa City, and they'll need to given how stout the Hawkeyes' run defense is. Iowa surrenders its most sacks yet Iowa Hawkeyes quarterback Jeremy Hecklinski. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Regardless of Hank Brown being announced as Iowa's starter , I expect to see both him and Jeremy Hecklinski for the Hawkeyes in this game. Both have struggled at various points throughout the season, and both struggled last week at Minnesota. Now, they get an even tougher test with this Badgers defense. Regardless of Hank Brown being announced as Iowa's starter , I expect to see both him and Jeremy Hecklinski for the Hawkeyes in this game. Both have struggled at various points throughout the season, and both struggled last week at Minnesota. Now, they get an even tougher test with this Badgers defense. But more specifically, I predict Wisconsin will sack Iowa three or more times. The Hawkeyes have been very strong in pass protection with just six sacks allowed all season, and they haven't let a team sack them more than twice in a game. I see that changing Saturday afternoon. Iowa's right tackle, Jack Dotzler, has been very good at times this fall. But he's also surrendered 12 pressures and two sacks, and now he has to line up against Sebastian Cheeks, who leads the Power Four in pressures with 35 and who just racked up 2.5 sacks last week against USC. Wisconsin's pass rush showed that it could both create pressure with four-man (and sometimes even three-man) fronts, while defensive coordinator Mike Tressel also displayed an ability to scheme up pressure against a complex and high-flying Trojans offense. The Badgers need that same level of defensive attention to detail this week. Accordingly, so has the tight end Jacob Harris, who burst onto the scene with a three-game stretch against Eastern Michigan, Penn State and Michigan State during which he caught 10 passes for 229 yards and three scores. Since the game against the Spartans, he has just three catches for 24 yards. Wisconsin's passing game has been nearly silent the past two weeks. Since the game against the Spartans, he has just three catches for 24 yards. As mentioned, Iowa's outside cornerbacks have been pretty tough to throw on, and Wisconsin doesn't have an elite separator at wideout, downfield or underneath, other than Malachi Coleman, who hasn't caught a pass since the Michigan State game and sat out against the Trojans (though he's probable to play this week). Thus, one of the ways offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes can kickstart this passing game is by getting Harris involved. The 6-6, 265-pound tight end is a mismatch for just about anyone on defense, and he has arguably the best hands on the Badgers. Grimes drew up a tunnel screen to him against the Trojans, which was snuffed out for no gain. But the point remains; getting Harris the ball could be a great way to get this passing game going. This week, the Hawkeyes should clean up those mistakes and be ready to take on a Wisconsin Badgers team coming off a big win over No. 16 USC. I wouldn't play this any higher than the current number. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brad Schultz · Roundtable Sports Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kirk Ferentz's perspective of the Iowa-Wisconsin rivalry When Iowa football fans glanced at the 2026 schedule in the summer, one of the games that they chalked up as likely wins was a Halloween contest against rival Wisconsin. And it made perfect sense back then. The Badger program was seemingly going nowhere under head coach Luke Fickell, and many people believed 2026 would be Fickell's final season before the school would cut ties with him. But flash-forward to Halloween, and Iowa and Wisconsin enter this matchup in completely different directions. The Hawkeyes are desperate for a bounce-back win after an ugly loss at Minnesota last weekend, while the Badgers could vault themselves into College Football Playoff contention with a victory (just check their schedule after the Iowa game). Every Iowa-Wisconsin game always seems to provide something unusual, so one can only imagine what will happen on Saturday. Here's my prediction for the matchup. Matchup: No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers (5-2, 3-1) @ Iowa Hawkeyes (5-2, 2-2) Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Scheduled game time: Oct. 31 at 11:10 a.m. Weather: 63 degrees Announcers: Gus Johnson (play-by-play), Joel Klatt (analyst), Jenny Taft (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Luke Jorden) I'm very surprised that Wisconsin is a competitive team at this point, but Iowa Everywhere's Chris Hassel said it best on Wednesday - the Badgers know their identity by now and the Hawkeyes don't. Iowa essentially using a roulette wheel to determine its starting quarterback each week has clearly caused this offense to be inconsistent week in and week out. Though Wisconsin hasn't received great quarterback play from Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph, it has relied on a good run game and excellent defense to win football games. Sticking to that strategy has worked well for the Badgers. All you have to do to figure that out is go back and watch their last game against USC. Wisconsin dominated both lines of scrimmage en route to a 24-7 victory last weekend and you better believe they'll try and do the same thing to Iowa. But can the Badgers actually come to Kinnick Stadium and pull this one out? The momentum is definitely on Wisconsin's side of the ball, but if there's one edge Iowa has, it's the fact that it's playing at Kinnick Stadium. The Badgers haven't won in Iowa City since 2018, with the Hawkeyes winning the last three games in Kinnick by a combined score of 94-27. I don't expect a lot of points to be scored in this one (stay tuned for my betting prediction later today), but if there's one thing I know about Kirk Ferentz, it's his ability to win these Big Ten grinders. He's going to try and flip the calendar back to 2023 and win this game with complimentary football. That wouldn't be a good strategy on the road, but I think this defense will feed off the home crowd and give their offense enough short fields to secure a narrow victory. The Hawkeyes take down Wisconsin for the sixth time in seven games. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 13

picks.blurb: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Wisconsin Badgers Game Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Wisconsin Badgers Game Preview David Fidler · SB Nation Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This Saturday, the 5-2 Iowa Hawkeyes are back at home in Kinnick Stadium to take on the 5-2 Wisconsin Badgers in the Battle for the Heartland Trophy. The Badgers, whose only losses are to ranked teams, are trending in the right direction while Iowa, which just lost to a mediocre Minnesota, is trending in the wrong direction. It's hard to know what to expect from the Hawkeyes going into this game. The team that embarrassed itself against the Gophers would lose to the Badgers and probably all the rest of the teams on its schedule. On the other hand, the team that showed up three weeks ago against the Washington Huskies would compete with the Badgers and have a reasonable chance of running the rest of the schedule. My guess is that the Hawkeyes that show up this week and for the rest of the year will be somewhere in the middle of those two extremes. Will the Hawkeyes Bounce Back? It is hard to remember Iowa looking more lackluster, more undisciplined, against an inferior opponent than it looked against Minnesota. It did almost everything it could to hand the game to the Gophers. The offense, to a man, looked unprepared. The special teams was uneven with a couple of huge gaffes. The defense did enough to win, but even Iowa's vaunted defense had at least two notable breakdowns. This game against the Badgers is important not only for Iowa's record, not only to preserve its slim playoff hopes, but it will also say what this team is made of. After a performance like the one against Minnesota, when everything was in the line, it would be easy enough for the Hawkeyes to give up on the season. On the other hand, they could also look adversity in the face and come out swinging. If the Hawkeyes show up flat again, it is entirely possible the season could spiral. Either way, there is a lot to answer for this week. Can Iowa Play a Clean Game? Iowa currently ranks 40th in the NCAA in penalty-yards-per-game. That's not terrible, but in 2025 the Hawkeyes were third. 2024: third. 2023 and 2022: fifth. 2021: sixth. 2020: 14th. You get the idea. Interestingly, the last time Iowa didn't finish the season in the top 25 of fewest penalty yards was 2015 when they went undefeated, but the 2026 Hawkeyes decidedly don't have CJ Beathard at quarterback. The larger point is that Iowa plays clean football. It is a hallmark of the program under Kirk Ferentz, and this incarnation of the Iowa Hawkeyes has not played clean football. It was evident against Minnesota, but it's been evident all season. And then there's turnover margin. After the garbage that was the Minnesota game, Iowa finds itself 80th in the country with a turnover margin of -1. The reality is Iowa can't sustain undisciplined, sloppy play. It can't give the opposing team free drives. It can't give the opposing team free yards. More than anything else, that needs to be cleaned up, and it needs to be cleaned up before anything else. As long as that is part of this team's DNA, it's not going to win football games. Who is the Quarterback and Can He Finish the Game? You've seen, and/or made your feelings known on the message boards. Hank Brown should have started, Jeremy Hecklinski should have never been benched, Heck should have come back in after Brown proved ineffective, etc. I have my opinions, but I don't know if it's the right choice any more than any of the others. What I do know is that Brown has had approximately five bad quarters in a row absent one drive. And against Minnesota, Heck was in his own head, making terrible decisions and starting to spiral. In short, Iowa seems to have two pretty poor quarterbacks that it has to decide between. Maybe that's why Ferentz has been so reticent to commit to one. Whomever the quarterback is, he doesn't need to be the second coming of Tom Brady. For the first time in a long time, Iowa has playmakers at receiver, not to mention the usual array of solid tight ends. All the quarterback has to do is make the makeables. When he has an open tight end in the seam on third-and-6, he has to hit him. When he has a receiver heading toward the end zone with five steps on his defender, he cannot underthrow him and give the defensive back a chance. He can't throw into double coverage. He can't hold the ball too long and take sacks. Given the running game, or lack thereof, a lot of weight is on the quarterback's shoulders, maybe too much. But with a good defense, all he has to do is consistently make the makeables. 2 Things to Watch Iowa fumbled five times vs Minnesota. Five?!?! Four were official and one didn't count due to a penalty. Okay, five was probably an anomaly, but at least one part of that equation is not an anomaly. Evan James, the punt returner, who fumbled the one against Minnesota that was called back due to a penalty, has fumbled three punts this season. He has fielded 32 punts. That means he's fumbling at a rate of almost 10% of his punts. Call me crazy but that is too much. I might be misremembering but I can swear Kirk Ferentz took Desmond King (Thorpe Award winner Desmond King!) off punt duties for flubbing a punt once during his sophomore year. Evan James has three fumbles, and he is still listed as the starting punt returner against Wisconsin. I'm all for Ferentz changing his approach to coaching here and there, but I don't think his leniency with fumbleitis is a positive development. It's hard to predict interceptions as the quarterback situation is still a bit hazy, but assuming it's Hank Brown, he did avoid the interception bug through the first four games, but since, he threw one against OSU and two against Minnesota. Then there's the defense. Look, the defense has done enough to win games—it certainly did enough against Minnesota—but it hasn't been generating a high number of turnovers. The Iowa defense has generated three interceptions against five Power-Four opponents this year. All of them have been by senior cornerback Deshaun Lee who, as I noted last week , is the only member of the secondary who is meeting the admittedly lofty expectations of an Iowa defensive back. This is a good week to generate turnovers as Wisconsin doesn't have a very good offense, and quarterback Colton Jones, though he is dangerous with his legs, is not a good passer. Jones has thrown five interceptions, but none in the last three games. However, that's largely because he hasn't put the ball in the air very much in the past three games, only averaging 16.7 attempts per game. The opportunities for interceptions should be there if Iowa can put the Badgers in a position where they have to throw the ball. I've already said that Iowa had to play a clean game. That includes winning the turnover battle. The Offensive Gameplan Iowa has played five Power-Four opponents. It has been able to run successfully and consistently against one of them. With a 20% success rate, I am going to assume Iowa will not be able to run the football using its base offense until proven otherwise. This is especially true after the announcement that starting tailback Kamari Moulton is out for the season. But the offense still needs to move the ball. Offenses typically have a play that the entire offense is built around. It's not the home run play or a play saved for special occasions. It's a bread-and-butter play that is run 5-15 times a game, is safe and nets consistent and dependable yardage. For Iowa, that play has historically been the inside zone, but it's not working, and as the Hawkeyes can't depend on big chunk plays through the passing game, they will need a play to build the offense around. So what's it going to be? Sweeps to the receivers, the screen game, the read option? None of it's ideal and it's not possible for Iowa to just scrap the inside zone, the foundation of its offense, in the middle of the season. However, running into a wall 5-10 times a game and averaging 1-2 yards per carry is not a winning formula, especially when the quarterbacks don't seem capable of carrying the offense on their shoulders. 1 Crazy Prediction I predict Iowa won't fumble the ball five times. Sounds like a pretty gutless prediction until you look at last week. But my serious prediction is that the Hawkeyes generate a non-offensive touchdown. Special teams? Maybe they keep the pick-6 streak alive? In truth, I think they might need it to win because I have no faith in this offense against a good Badger defense.

Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images (Matt Krohn, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 21 Iowa football releases Week 9 depth chart vs. Wisconsin Iowa football releases Week 9 depth chart vs. Wisconsin Iowa football vs. Minnesota: Best photos from Week 8 'Not good enough': Kirk Ferentz laments Iowa's QB play vs. Minnesota CBS shares Iowa football bowl projection after Minnesota loss Iowa football plummets in updated US LBM Coaches Poll rankings Iowa football falls out of latest AP Top 25 poll rankings Josh Helmer: Iowa has owned this series of late, winning each of the past four and outscoring the Badgers during that stretch, 118-26. I just don't see Saturday playing out in a similar, lopsided fashion. This will be your typical grind-it-out, lean on the defense and special teams, field position battle. Two great defenses take the field in this contest: Wisconsin and Iowa rank 13th and 14th nationally in total defense. The Hawkeyes are No. 8 in scoring defense (14.3 points per game), while the Badgers rank No. 12 (15.3 points per game). Iowa's quarterback questions have reemerged after Jeremy Hecklinski was benched last week in favor of former starter Hank Brown. There's run game concerns for Iowa, too. Leading rusher Kamari Moulton is out for the remainder of the season, and this Hawkeye offense hasn't generated much of anything on the ground against power foes outside of its win at Washington . Iowa wins, but it's on the backs of the Hawkeyes' defense and special teams. Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13 Scout Springgate: In a sport that has already delivered incredible moments so far this year, the battle for the Heartland Trophy between Iowa and Wisconsin has suddenly become extremely important for both sides. For Iowa, it's a must-win game after an abysmal offensive showing at Minnesota last week. Looking ahead, Iowa travels to a rowdy Ryan Field to face a red-hot Northwestern program next week and needs this win to avoid heading there on a two-game losing streak and with its CFP hopes completely dashed. In what should be a low-scoring defensive battle, it will come down to whether Iowa can capitalize on their scoring opportunities and sustain enough drives where they don't hang their defense out to dry. With the game in front of a sold-out Kinnick Stadium, I feel confident Iowa can pull out a victory over Wisconsin by making critical defensive plays and having the offense do just enough to win. However, I don't foresee the Hawkeyes necessarily answering the litany of questions and concerns on offense with their performance. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 10 Zach Hiney: It's funny how quickly things can change in sports. Just one week ago, Iowa was 5-1, and many thought they had a shot at making the College Football Playoff. Now, the general mood within the fanbase is very negative following a poor showing in a loss to Minnesota. Playoff hopes are dashed, and questions at quarterback have popped back up. In addition to their own internal issues, the Hawkeyes will also have to contend with a hot Wisconsin team on Saturday. The Badgers are coming off a big home win over USC and are playing their best football in years. New quarterback Colton Joseph didn't do much against the Trojans, but has largely been a positive this season. He has 15 total touchdowns and is a dangerous dual-threat option. Wisconsin's defense has been stellar recently, giving up only 27 total points in their last three games. That includes a dominant performance against USC, where they held the high-powered Trojans to just seven points. Now they'll get to play an Iowa offense in complete disarray. Hank Brown will start at quarterback, but his effectiveness will be the big question. He'll have to operate without leading rusher Kamari Moulton, who's out for the season with an injury. I don't have a lot of confidence in Iowa's offense at the moment. The Moulton injury is a big blow. I envision that unit having some problems on Saturday. But I do have a lot of confidence in Phil Parker's defense. Joseph is a fine quarterback, but he's the kind of guy Iowa has made its hay against during Parker's tenure. I expect the Hawkeyes' defense to turn in another strong performance. Throw in the fact that this game is at Kinnick Stadium, and I feel decent about Iowa's chances. The Hawkeyes win, but don't answer many of the questions about their offense in the process. The Badgers have trotted out five different starting combinations along the offensive front through seven games this season. Wisconsin's initial injury report was mostly status quo, except for one surprising inclusion. Fifth-year senior offensive lineman Barrett Nelson, who started for the Badgers at right guard in Week 8 in the win over No. 16 USC, was listed as doubtful on the Wednesday night injury report. He and running back Nate Palmer, who hasn't played since Week 5 against Michigan State, are the two Badgers with a "doubtful" designation ahead of the enormous showdown with Iowa in Week 9. But if Nelson is unavailable, Wilkins would likely be forced back into the starting five, as Wisconsin has shown it doesn't want to play backup center Ryan Cory (who replaced injured starter Austin Kawecki in the second half of the Michigan State game, and played well in the process) and would rather kick Stylz Blackmon over to center than have Cory start a game there. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Predictions: Our Staff Picks the Winner and Final Score
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Predictions: Our Staff Picks the Winner and Final Score Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 12 Ole Miss is playing back in Oxford on Halloween weekend to take on an Auburn team in the midst of its first season led by Alex Golesh. Both teams are entering Week 9 coming off losses, but it’s the Rebels that are playing with pressure for their playoff lives moving forward. Though Auburn is sitting at 4-3 (2-3) through what’s been an up and down season up to this point, the Tigers are no slouch. Just two weeks ago Auburn went into Athens and pulled out a last-second win over Georgia. Kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 11:45 a.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss will enter game day as a double-digit home favorite. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Oct 24, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) warms up before the game against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Not that it matters by any means, but aside from its impressive road win against Georgia two weeks ago, nothing particularly jumps off the page to me about Alex Golesh’s first team at Auburn. That’s not to say Golesh isn’t the right fit for the job either. He has the Tigers sitting above .500 and is working through his first season as a head coach at a Power Four program. As it pertains to the game itself, I expect Ole Miss to maintain its home win streak that dates back to September of the 2024 season. This certainly should be a focused group after picking up its second loss in Texas last weekend and they can’t afford to overlook Auburn even though Georgia is around the corner. Controlling their playoff destiny is on thin ice. Trinidad Chambliss could use a bounce back game after not looking like himself the past two weeks. Considering Auburn’s weaker pass defense through its secondary, I believe Chambliss does what he desperately needs to do and may even incorporate his legs more than usual. Ole Miss needs to prove it can find a faster start on the offensive side of the ball as a whole. Defensively, Ole Miss should match up well against an offense that has already surrendered 29 sacks (4.3 per game) if the unit can contain Byrum Brown. The Tigers’ quarterback leads the team in rushing yards, but still looks like a signal-caller in his first season in the SEC. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 17 While Auburn is more than capable of pulling off the upset, just look at its victory over No. 3 Georgia in Athens, I don’t see it happening this Saturday. Against Texas, the Ole Miss offense did everything it could to let Texas pull away. However, despite struggling for most of the night, they lost the game by just seven points. The two games prior to Texas, Ole Miss won by blowing out its opponents. With the Rebels’ back against the wall and needing to go on a win streak if they want to make the College Football Playoff, I think they win easily against Auburn and carry some nice momentum into their matchup against the Georgia Bulldogs next Saturday night. Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 Cooper Ferguson Alex Golesh will take this Auburn team to greener pastures than Hugh Freeze ever did, and I think that in the alternate universe where Golesh came to Auburn, things worked out. A great coach tasked with waking a sleeping giant, I think Auburn will, in due time, become a force to be reckoned with again in the SEC. That time is not now, though. Florida and the first half against Texas need to be remembered as blips in a strong season for the Rebels in years to come. With a strong showing against Auburn this Halloween, Ole Miss will be well on its way to correcting its path. Chambliss and Co. dispatch the Tigers easily, and Ole Miss moves on to prep for Georgia. Ole Miss 49, Auburn 14 Billy Flowers Byrum Brown will be a major problem for the Ole Miss run defense, but Auburn's offensive line is horrific. I think the Tigers' only path to victory is through Brown's legs, which, frankly, will not put enough points on the board for Auburn. I think Trinidad bounces back, and Makhai Frazier has a breakout performance against the Tiger's less-than-stellar rush defense. I do think Auburn can keep the game close, thanks to their rushing attack. The Ole Miss offense is too talented, and the Tigers won't score enough to match it. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off a disappointing performance against Texas and really needs a solid response this week. The key to victory is to keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. The Auburn quarterback can make big plays with his legs, so limiting his mobility will be a priority. The Tigers knocked off Georgia a couple of weeks ago, but I think Pete Golding’s team responds well at home. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24 The Ole Miss Rebels face a must-win game against the Auburn Tigers. They won't disappoint. Auburn is a dangerous football team, but Ole Miss will show its talent when it needs to. Trinidad Chambliss will have a day as the defense struggles at first but settles in. The Rebels, in the end, will win this game by three-plus touchdowns. Ole Miss 45, Auburn 24 Published Oct 30, 2026 TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Ole Miss against Auburn Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Today at 11:45 a.m. CT, the No. 12 Ole Miss Rebels play the Auburn Tigers at home . Both teams are looking to bounce back following losses. Auburn lost 38-17 last Saturday to the No. 15 LSU Tigers. Ole Miss lost 34-27 to the No. 11 Texas Longhorns last Saturday. Both teams were coming off victories over ranked opponents the week before their losses and are looking to reignite the momentum they had prior to last week's losses. With the stage set, let's get into my three bold predictions for the game. 1. Trinidad Chambliss Has No Turnovers Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss throws a pass during the first quarter against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been very efficient this season. However, there is one lingering issue standing out on his stat sheet: he keeps turning the ball over. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been very efficient this season. However, there is one lingering issue standing out on his stat sheet: he keeps turning the ball over. Chambliss has thrown an interception in all but two games this season. He's also fumbled four times, although only two led to turnovers. Texas was the worst game so far this season for interceptions, as he threw three of them, although the last was on a Hail Mary as time expired. Chambliss has been great aside from the turnovers, as he's scored 22 touchdowns and has over 2,000 combined yards. However, the Rebels need to go on a winning streak to make the College Football Playoff, and Chambliss' turnover issues will stop that from happening if they are not improved immediately. I expect that improvement to start against Auburn. 2. Backup Running Backs Show Flashes Mississippi Rebels running back Makhi Frazier carries the ball during the second half against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A major concern heading into this matchup, and potentially the rest of the season, is who can step up for Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy now that he's missing time with a dislocated shoulder . A major concern heading into this matchup, and potentially the rest of the season, is who can step up for Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy now that he's missing time with a dislocated shoulder . Running backs Makhi Frazier , JT Lindsey and Shekai Mills-Knight have been mentioned as players with opportunities to fill Lacy's role in the offense. I expect Ole Miss to utilize a rotation of rushers against Auburn, which likely lowers the ceiling of any running back's individual performance. However, that doesn't mean that one or more of them won't impress on Saturday. I expect a rushing touchdown or two from the committee and an impressive yards per carry average, even if it's unlikely for any of them to break the 100-yard rushing mark. 3. Defense Limits Byrum Brown Mississippi Rebels safety Andy Jaffe celebrates with safety Anthony Robinson III after recovering an onside kick during the second half against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown leads his team in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, alongside his more than 1,300 passing yards and eight passing touchdowns. It's no exaggeration to say he's been nearly the entire offense. Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown leads his team in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, alongside his more than 1,300 passing yards and eight passing touchdowns. It's no exaggeration to say he's been nearly the entire offense. However, against LSU last week, he just couldn't get anything going. He finished the game with 160 passing yards for no passing touchdowns, as well as 20 rushing yards on 19 rushes for one touchdown. While Ole Miss' defense hasn't been fantastic this season at defending mobile quarterbacks, I expect the Rebels' defense to return to the level they played at against Vanderbilt and No. 23 Missouri. In those two games, the opposing teams scored just 20 combined points against Ole Miss. The performance against Texas wasn't all bad for the defense, but heading into the final stretch of the season, where things have to go right for the Rebels, I think the defense makes its presence felt for the whole game instead of just in moments. Who does ESPN have winning when Auburn travels to Ole Miss on Saturday? According to the ESPN Matchup Predictor , Auburn has a 25.1% chance of picking up a victory at Ole Miss. The Tigers have not lost back-to-back games this season and will be looking to avoid that in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday. It will be a tall task for Auburn to come away with a win over the Rebels, who are coming off a narrow defeat last week at the hands of the Texas Longhorns . Ole Miss almost made a huge comeback after trailing Texas 24-3 at halftime. Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss could not find the end zone as time expired, and Ole Miss lost 34-27. At 5-2, Ole Miss can not afford another loss if they want to make the College Football Playoff. This will be the first meeting between the two schools since the 2023 season , when Ole Miss defeated Auburn in the first year of the Hugh Freeze era. These two programs met each year when they were both part of the SEC West division. Auburn leads the all-time series 35-12, but Ole Miss has won the last two meetings. In the final five games of the season, Auburn should be able to snap their streak of five consecutive losing seasons. With four wins, Auburn should be able to get three more victories with games against Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford. A matchup that could help Auburn pull off an upset victory over Ole Miss is in the run game. The Rebels are at the bottom of the SEC, giving up 161.1 yards per game on the ground. Saturday could be an opportunity for Byrum Brown and the Auburn running backs to have a big game. picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn: Can the Rebels bounce back and save their College Football Playoff hopes? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Final Score predictions for Ole Miss Rebels and Auburn Tigers Scott Wachter-Imagn Images and John Reed-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:54 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ole Miss Rebels are in a position to bounce back against an Auburn team that looked bad last week. The Ole Miss Rebels lost to the Texas Longhorns last week. The loss does not help their College Football Playoff chances at all. In fact, they now have a 44% chance of making the postseason. A win over the Auburn Tigers on Saturday would move that to 53%, according to A to Z's Simulator. As for Auburn, they have a 1% chance to make it . And, with a win over Ole Miss, that jumps to just 7%. They then have to play Alabama in Week 13, too. This could be a great game with real implications. So, our experts broke it all down. Final Score Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn Ole Miss 34, Auburn 16: Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame Ole Miss takes care of business against Auburn with a 34-16 win, thanks largely to a monster performance from quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Kewan Lacy sidelined, the Rebels needed someone to step up offensively, and Chambliss delivered. He makes plays with both his arm and his legs, keeping Auburn's defense on its heels and helping Ole Miss avoid a major drop-off without one of its key offensive weapons. The Rebels find success through the air and do enough on the ground to keep the offense balanced, putting Auburn in a difficult spot for most of the afternoon. Auburn's offensive struggles continue as the Tigers struggle to put together consistent drives against an Ole Miss defense that takes advantage of their mistakes. The Tigers may find a few scoring chances, but they lack the consistency to make this a competitive second half. As Auburn's offense stalls, Chambliss and the Rebels capitalize, gradually building a comfortable lead and putting the game out of reach. Ole Miss leaves with a 34-16 win, and Chambliss proves he can carry a significant portion of the offensive load even without Lacy in the lineup. Ole Miss 35, Auburn 20: Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama After a big win over Georgia a couple of weeks ago, the Tigers came back to Earth against LSU last weekend, and things won't get any easier against Ole Miss this week. The Rebels will look to bounce back after a loss to the Longhorns, with their playoff lives on the line. I don't know how Auburn plans to contain Trinidad Chambliss, but he'll be back and hungry to make plays after a down performance against Texas. An Auburn defense that has struggled for much of the season may be the perfect scenario for this team and Trinidad Chambliss. Give me Ole Miss by a wide margin. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24: Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida I was high on Auburn after their upset win over Georgia and genuinely thought they'd beat the LSU Tigers. Well, they instead got smoked and got exposed as not ready to compete. Ole Miss is now on life support in the playoff race, having lost to Florida and Texas, two other SEC foes who also have two losses. Trinidad Chambliss was very inconsistent against the Longhorns and will use this as a get-right game for the stretch run. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 23: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee In a game the Rebels cannot afford to lose to stay in the playoff picture, it starts with a bit of a scare. Byrum Brown and the Tigers get off to another strong road start, building an early lead and leaning on the ground game to shorten the game and keep Trinidad Chambliss on the sideline longer than Rebel fans want. But the Rebels get things going quickly in the second half. As Sam Leavitt and the Tigers did from the jump last week against Auburn, Chambliss and his targets get in rhythm and push ahead in the third quarter. Auburn keeps it interesting until the end, but they can't pull off the big road upset for the second time in as many tries. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Alex Golesh Delivers Positive News Regarding Injured Auburn Tigers in Ole Miss Loss
away.blurb: The Auburn Tigers saw several of their key defensive pieces go d own in the loss to No. 12 Ole Miss this past weekend in Oxford. However, head coach Alex Golesh was optimistic about their returns soon. Speaking to the media for the first time since the weekend, Golesh mentioned that cornerbacks Newboy Fegans, Andre Jordan Jr . and safety Sylvester Smith-Reed practiced on Monday, meaning the injuries were short-term. However, there won’t be an official answer on whether they’ll be ready to play against Arkansas until later this week. “I think we’ll have a way better feel on Wednesday, and I’ll update you all on Wednesday on the injury side of it,” Golesh said. As for the secondary, as a whole, there’s a lot to assess on Auburn’s side of things eight games into the season. There’s the positive side of it: when the Tigers are getting tackles for loss and sacks, the secondary plays better and complementary. Golesh hasn’t seen any issues when that is happening. Auburn has the third-most interceptions in the SEC this season with nine , only being behind the likes of Alabama and Tennessee. “When everybody’s on the same page, and we’re playing ahead of the sticks, we’ve been sound,” he said. However, there have been recent issues since Auburn’s win against No. 1 Georgia in the middle of the month. The Tigers gave up 387 and 263 yards to LSU and Ole Miss, respectively, in the last two games, leading to losses by multiple touchdowns. Golesh’s defense is allowing over 252 yards per game through the air this season, which is second-to-last in the conference. The head coach has seen ups and downs throughout the season, saying nerves could settle in at times in the secondary. "I think at times, played well, and then at times there have been some panicky moments. To me, you give up a go-ball, guy goes up and over, those are moments you can live with,” he said. “I think when there are some communication things, that’s where I struggle with.” A benefit from the loss to Ole Miss, as well as the three players going down above, was that a younger group of defensive backs was able to get notable playing time in the game. Names like sophomore Blake Woodby, USF transfer Fred Gaskin and Florida State transfer Shamar Arnoux all got extended time, among others. away.blurb: The Tigers record took a beating from the game, but so did its secondary, which suffered from injuries throughout the matchup. Safety Sylvester Smith-Reed, nickel AnQuon "Newboy" Fegans and cornerback Andre Jordan Jr. were all sideline throughout various points of Saturday's game, but according to head coach Alex Golesh, all three players were out on the field practicing on Monday. Starting corner Jordan exited the game after just three plays and did not return to the game, and Fegans seemed to be dealing with a leg injury before heading out of the game in the second quarter. Smith-Reed left the game after a pass breakup in the second half. At the tail end of the season, in the midst of the brutal play in the SEC, Golesh know that depth is an important factor in finishing strong. Also with the potential to return to action this weekend is sophomore wide receiver Jeremiah Koger. Golesh said he was close to be able to play against Ole Miss but was ultimately ruled out, and the Tigers hope to have him back against Arkansas. home.blurb: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM Koger was listed as questionable on the Tigers’ initial injury report Thursday meaning that he has around a 50% chance to play, while offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are listed as out. At this time, it is unclear as to why exactly Koger is listed as questionable, but it goes without saying that losing his production would be a significant blow for the Tigers, as he currently ranks third among all Tigers in total receiving yards. Koger was a four-star recruit out of St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, Maryland, when he signed with Alex Golesh and the USF Bulls, earning playing time quite early in his young career. Last season, his freshman year, Koger hauled in 38 Byrum Brown passes for 597 yards and eight touchdowns before transferring to the Plains this past offseason. If Koger is ruled out for the game against Ole Miss, the Tigers still have plenty of other talent to turn to in the interim, including fellow USF transfer receiver Christian Neptune, who completed a touchdown pass to Singleton against Georgia, as well as DeShawn Spencer, a true freshman who has hauled in 10 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns so far this season. The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound from a devastating loss to LSU, in which the Bayou Bengals came to town and routed the home team by 21 points, though that effort may get a little more difficult with the potential absence of one key wide receiver: Jeremiah Koger. The Maryland native was highly anticipated on the Plains and has lived up to a large part of those expectations, though he has not yet quite turned in the statistical production of the Tigers’ top two receivers, Keshaun Singleton and Chas Nimrod, both of whom are also new Auburn transfers from USF. So far this season, Koger has caught 14 passes for 230 yards, both stats ranking third on the team. Notably, however, Koger has yet to bring in a touchdown for the Tigers this year, which is quite surprising given his production at USF last season. Singleton and Nimrod have worked to make up for that, though, hauling in a combined five touchdown passes from Brown this season. They’ve also combined for 69 total receptions and 771 receiving yards, a high mark for any Auburn duo. The Tigers are scheduled to square off against Ole Miss this Saturday, October 31, at 11:45 a.m. CT, in a matchup that is scheduled to be broadcast on SEC Network. picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odds have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: Aaron Murray Reveals His Score Prediction For Georgia-Florida Game
picks.blurb: Aaron Murray Reveals His Score Prediction For Georgia-Florida Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS One of college football's biggest rivalries takes center stage Saturday afternoon when No. 3 Georgia and No. 17 Florida square off in a matchup with major SEC and College Football Playoff implications. The Bulldogs (6-1) are looking to bounce back from a stunning 27-24 loss to Auburn, while the Gators (5-2) are hoping to build on their impressive road victory over Texas. With plenty on the line for both programs, former Georgia quarterback and current SEC Network analyst Aaron Murray has weighed in with his prediction for Saturday's showdown. During a recent episode of the Aaron Murray College Football Show , Murray broke down the matchup before ultimately picking his former team to come out on top. "The Dawgs win 35 to 27," Murray predicted. Aaron Murray Expects Gunner Stockton to Bounce Back Against Florida Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect One of Murray's biggest reasons for picking Georgia is his confidence in Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton. One of Murray's biggest reasons for picking Georgia is his confidence in Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton. Stockton struggled with turnovers in Georgia's loss to Auburn, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble that helped set up the Tigers' game-winning field goal. However, Murray believes those mistakes were an exception rather than a sign of bigger problems. Murray also pointed to Florida's struggling secondary as a potential opportunity for Stockton to put together a big performance. The Gators are allowing approximately 255 passing yards per game, something Murray believes Georgia can exploit with its talented group of receivers. He also emphasized the importance of Florida winning the battle at the line of scrimmage. If the Gators cannot generate pressure on Stockton, Murray expects the Bulldogs' offense to have a productive afternoon. Georgia-Florida Matchup Carries Major SEC Playoff Implications USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Saturday's rivalry game is about much more than bragging rights. Saturday's rivalry game is about much more than bragging rights. Georgia enters the weekend with a 4-1 SEC record and remains firmly in the conference championship race despite its recent setback against Auburn. Florida, meanwhile, sits at 3-2 in conference play and has little room for another loss if it hopes to remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. A Georgia victory would strengthen the Bulldogs' position in the SEC race while delivering a significant blow to Florida's postseason hopes. However, a Gators upset would create another major shakeup in an already unpredictable SEC championship race. The longtime rivals will meet at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta rather than their traditional Jacksonville location due to ongoing stadium renovations. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.
