For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated this afternoon at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites on Saturday, Oct. 31, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). Georgia -11.5 Georgia fourth quarter -2.5 Florida vs Georgia prop: Georgia team total Over 34.5 Florida's defense has been the death of it this season, allowing 34.2 points per game against SEC opponents. With Georgia averaging 33.6 points per game in SEC play, I like the Over on the Bulldogs' team total at 34.5 or better . The Gators have played four quarterbacks who rank top 50 nationally in QBR this season; in those four games, they've allowed an average of 37.5 points per game , with three of four opponents scoring 38+ points. Georgia's Gunner Stockton has the highest QBR of any quarterback Florida has seen this year, ranking No. 4 in the country (86.0). That doesn't bode well for a Gators defense that ranks 113th in EPA per dropback. While EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovation, the game is taking a two game hiatus from Duval County. The game will take place in Mercedes-Benz stadium in Atlanta on Saturday. Depending on the weather, the roof could be closed, hence the party being inside. This will be a very different atmosphere for this historic rivalry. Now, Florida fans will see that Jacksonville is not that neutral of a site. Atlanta is the equivalent in Georgia. So, that means some ridiculous things could happen Saturday afternoon. Here are three bold predictions for Saturday: Gunner Stockton Totals 4 Touchdowns Gunner Stockton is coming off of the worst game of his life, where he turned the ball over three times for the first time in his career, including the untimely fumble at the end of the game. That fumble led to Auburn's game-winning field goal. Florida has the second worst passing defense in the SEC. Stockton is one of the best and most efficient quarterbacks in the nation. A bounce back game seems likely, and he will total at least four scores. Georgia Wins Turnover Margin by 2 The Dawgs lost the turnover battle to Auburn 0-3, and they almost won. Georgia has been better about creating turnover opportunities this year than it was last season. Georgia has also had a knack for winning games despite losing the turnover battle. This game last year is an example of that. Georgia is due for a big turnover game. The Dawgs only have two takeaways over the last three games. Jadan Baugh Gets His Jadan Baugh is arguably college football's best running back. He has simmered down since his 600-yard and 11-touchdown start over the first four games. Rushing for over 90 yards and a score en route to an upset road win over Texas can be considered a bounce back. Georgia's run defense has progressively gotten worse as the season has gone on. Alabama was able to rip off some expl;osive and total about 160 yards on the ground. Byrum Brown ran all over the Dawgs, helping Auburn total over 190 rushing yards. Baugh is good enough to get his. Georgia is good enough to win even if that happens. I think he will have around 100 total yards and a score. picks.blurb: Tim Tebow lone Florida pick as ESPN panels favor Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Tim Tebow lone Florida pick as ESPN panels favor Georgia Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia has the overwhelming support of ESPN's pregame analysts ahead of Saturday's rivalry showdown with Florida , but one former Gators quarterback isn't following the crowd. Seven of the eight analysts who made predictions across College GameDay and SEC Nation picked the No. 3 Bulldogs to defeat No. 20 Florida at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Tim Tebow was the lone dissenting voice, backing his alma mater despite acknowledging several advantages for Georgia. The predictions come as both programs return from their bye weeks. Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) looks to build on its 27-24 upset victory over Texas, while Georgia (6-1, 4-1) tries to recover from a 27-24 loss to Auburn. College GameDay picks Georgia unanimously ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from Bloomington, Indiana, ahead of the Hoosiers' matchup with Minnesota. The panel unanimously selected Georgia to beat Florida, with Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee, and celebrity guest picker Isiah Thomas all siding with the Bulldogs. Kirk Herbstreit did not make a prediction because he is calling the game for ABC alongside Chris Fowler. The show's fan poll also heavily favored Georgia, with 76% of respondents picking the Bulldogs. Here's how the College GameDay panel voted: Desmond Howard: Georgia Nick Saban: Georgia Pat McAfee: Georgia Isiah Thomas: Georgia Kirk Herbstreit: No pick Tim Tebow stands alone on SEC Nation The SEC Nation crew broadcast from Atlanta, where Paul Finebaum, Roman Harper and Chase Daniel all picked Georgia. Tebow was the only panelist to give Florida the nod. Finebaum expressed little uncertainty about the matchup. "Georgia is really good. Florida is a mystery," Finebaum said. "This is not a difficult pick at all. The Dogs are going to win it." Harper acknowledged that Florida has a path to victory, particularly if the Gators utilize both Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. at quarterback, but ultimately sided with Georgia because of his confidence in Kirby Smart. Tebow appeared to reach the same conclusion. He praised Smart as the nation's best coach, described Georgia as the country's most complete team and highlighted quarterback Gunner Stockton as a major advantage for the Bulldogs. However, the former Florida quarterback shifted his focus to the emotion surrounding the rivalry and the people who make college football meaningful. After reflecting on a feature about Jadan Baugh and personal connections to the game, Tebow emphatically picked Florida to pull off the upset. Here's how the SEC Nation panel voted: Paul Finebaum: Georgia Roman Harper: Georgia Chase Daniel: Georgia Tim Tebow: Florida Florida and Georgia kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday on ABC. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the great college football rivalry games will be renewed this weekend as Georgia and Florida square off. And there's plenty on the line for both SEC hopeful teams. Georgia has won five straight against the Gators, but is coming off a surprise loss to unranked Auburn as the No. 1 team in the country. New head coach Jon Sumrall has rejuvenated the Florida program in many ways. But he also has two costly losses on the books already and is desperate to avoid a third. What happens when the Bulldogs and Gators renew their rivalry on Saturday? How Georgia can win Apr 18, 2026; Athens, GA, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) passes the ball during the Georgia Spring football game at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Georgia is the more balanced team statistically on both sides of the ball, but one major advantage still sticks out. Florida's secondary is allowing 255 yards in the air per game and is struggling badly to get off the field on third down this season. The unit ranks second-worst among SEC teams in both categories. Georgia's offense, meanwhile, is third and first in the conference on those scores, respectively. Exploiting these relative weaknesses will be critical. If quarterback Gunner Stockton can stay efficient and the Bulldogs can better establish the run game, they have the ingredients to control this matchup. More: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 9's biggest games How Florida can win Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Florida Gators running back Jadan Baugh (13) celebrates with a Heisman pose against the Mississippi Rebels during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Running the ball with authority and winning the turnover battle is key. Georgia's run defense is pretty solid overall, but has been a little leaky the last two times out. It allowed almost 6 yards per carry from Alabama's backs in a close win, and surrendered almost 200 yards total from Auburn in the upset. Florida ranks No. 10 in time of possession courtesy of a backfield that has proven it can take over games. More: 4 bold college football predictions for Week 9's biggest games The Gators place fourth in the SEC in rushing output and Jon Sumrall-coached teams have won 37 of their last 40 games when they run for 125 yards. If they can win the possession battle and capitalize on scoring opportunities, they have the offensive talent to make this more than competitive. More: One glaring matchup Florida can exploit against Georgia Who wins, and why? Florida is expected to start Aaron Philo at quarterback after an injury-induced absence, but the Georgia front has the bodies to apply enough pressure to contain him in the pocket and rush his decisions. And while the Gators have shown they can run on quality defenses, like in a win at Texas last time out, they've also shown that opponents can bottle them up just as easily. Georgia's front definitely leans on the latter, and combined with the skill targets to outrace a vulnerable Florida secondary, that should be enough to determine this one down the stretch. The Big Lead prediction: Georgia 33, Florida 21

picks.headline: College Football Week 9 Expert Picks, Predictions For Florida-Georgia And More
picks.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores SPORTS & TEAMS PERSONALITIES POPULAR SEARCHES College Football Add FOX Sports on Google College Football Week 9 Expert Picks, Predictions For Florida-Georgia And More Updated Oct. 30, 2026 8:56 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Laken Litman College Football and Soccer Writer RJ Young College Football Writer Ben Portnoy College Sports Writer Week 8 of the college football season matched the chaos in Weeks 6 and 7. Can Week 9 make that four in a row? Saturday starts with No. 25 Wisconsin, ranked for the first time since 2023, taking its College Football Playoff hopes to Kinnick Stadium, facing Iowa on "Big Noon Kickoff." Meanwhile, No. 13 Texas Tech will try to avoid plummeting after a surprising loss to Cincinnati when it faces No. 22 Arizona. In the afternoon, can No. 17 Florida secure its third upset of a top-5 team this season against No. 3 Georgia? Will No. 6 Utah remain perfect against the surging Bearcats? The night ends with Lincoln Riley's coaching for his job, while No. 2 Ohio State tries to keep its season alive after losing quarterback Julian Sayin. We're breaking down our straight-up picks and the matchups to watch closely throughout the weekend. Iowa vs. No. 25 Wisconsin Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph set the record for most rushing yards by a Badgers quarterback when he posted 141 against Michigan State. (Photo by Lawrence Iles/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX) Where: Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City, Iowa Line: Iowa -3.5 RJ Young: Wisconsin If Wisconsin can keep Lincoln Riley's offense at bay, there's no reason to believe it can't do the same to Iowa. Laken Litman: Wisconsin After spending some time on the hot seat, Luke Fickell's team maintains momentum on the road against an Iowa team which has lost two of its last three. Ben Portnoy: Wisconsin Wisconsin has found new life thanks to a retooled NIL operation and a roster that now more closely matches that of its Big Ten brethren. If the Badgers get through this one, it might be time to start thinking about a College Football Playoff game in Madison. No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita threw for 308 yards and one touchdown as the Wildcats dominated Iowa State in Week 8. (Photo by Christopher Hook/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ESPN) Where: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, Texas Line: Texas Tech -3.5 Young: Arizona When Noah Fifita is playing at his best, the Wildcats look like a team capable of winning the Big 12 championship. Litman: Arizona In a wild and crazy Big 12, Arizona goes into Lubbock and gets the win behind a big performance from quarterback Noah Fifita. Portnoy: Arizona Arizona has quietly been one of the best teams nobody is talking about. Noah Fifita continues to be a star for the Wildcats. After last week's debacle at Cincinnati, I'm skeptical Texas Tech has enough offensively to win this one. No. 12 Ole Miss vs. Auburn Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss threw for 250 yards, but the Rebels second-half comeback fell short against Texas in Week 8. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 12:45 p.m. ET (ESPN) Where: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford, Mississippi Line: Ole Miss -13.5 Young: Ole Miss Trinidad Chambliss is the closest player college football has to New York Knicks' guard Jalen Brunson and his clutch ability late in games. Litman: Ole Miss The Rebels bounce back at home and keep their CFP hopes alive. Portnoy: Ole Miss I know Auburn beat Georgia two weeks ago, but that came on the heels of a handful of lucky breaks that have made us think differently about this team. Simply put, Ole Miss is better in every facet right now and should win going away. No. 3 Georgia vs. No. 17 Florida Gunner Stockton and Georgia are trying to bounce back from a loss against Auburn in Week 7, coming off their bye. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta, Georgia Line: Georgia -11.5 Young: Georgia The Gators are banged up at quarterback and wide receiver. Litman: Georgia The Bulldogs are rejuvenated after a bye week following their first loss of the season and will leave no doubt in this rivalry matchup. Portnoy: Florida I am still not quite sure what to make of Florida, but given the offensive upside, the Gators don't need to be that effective to get a win here. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton was susceptible to turnovers against Auburn. Florida's defense isn't as good, but weird things happen in this rivalry. Oregon vs. No. 20 Northwestern David Braun has Northwestern football in the Associated Press Top 25 for the first season since 2020. (Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (Peacock) Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, Oregon Line: Oregon -3.5 Young: Northwestern The Wildcats are healthier than the Ducks by a fair margin. Litman: Northwestern Northwestern gets a massive road win against a struggling Oregon offense that is desperately missing quarterback Dante Moore. Portnoy: Northwestern Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly should probably be the front-runner for the Broyles Award, honoring the best assistant coach in America. The Ducks are in the midst of a lost season and a slew of off-the-field issues have vibes at the lowest they've been in years around the program. Give me the 'Cats to keep in the mix for a CFP berth. Cincinnati vs. No. 6 Utah Utah quarterback Devon Dampier rushed for 150 yards and two touchdowns in the Utes win over Houston in Week 8. (Photo by Chris Gardner/ Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:45 p.m. ET (ESPN) Where: Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati, Ohio Line: Utah -6.5 Young: Utah The Bearcats will fall against a program as good at running the football as they are. Litman: Utah Cincinnati is coming off a huge win against Texas Tech, but Utah keeps its perfect season intact. Portnoy: Utah Utah finally played an opponent with a pulse last week and gave us enough evidence to suggest it and BYU should be considered the frontrunners for the Big 12 title this year. Cincinnati shouldn't be overlooked after throttling Texas Tech, but the high of that win feels hard to shake off with a trip out West on tap. Iowa State vs. No. 24 Oklahoma State Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker threw for 386 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys win over Colorado in Week 8. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:00 p.m. ET (FS1) Where: Jack Trice Stadium, Ames, Iowa Line: Oklahoma State -8.5 Young: Oklahoma State Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker is playing like a Heisman Trophy finalist. Litman: Oklahoma State Drew Mestemaker is having one of the best seasons of any quarterback in the nation and that continues against the struggling Cyclones. Portnoy: Oklahoma State I've admittedly fallen victim to forgetting about Oklahoma State for long stretches after the loss to Tulsa. Hard to ignore now. Drew Mestemaker is playing as well as any quarterback in America. That's the difference in this one. USC vs. No. 2 Ohio State Ohio State head coach Ryan Day has a decision to make, choosing a new starting quarterback after Julian Sayin's injury. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC) Where: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, California Line: USC -6.5 Young: Ohio State The Buckeyes possess the better defense and the best player in the sport in wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Litman: Ohio State Even without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, the Buckeyes show their resilience and make life for USC coach Lincoln Riley that much harder. Portnoy: Ohio State Is it Tavien St. Clair or Luke Fahey at quarterback for the Buckeyes? Perhaps both? I'm skeptical of how far this Ohio State team can go without Julian Sayin, but USC feels like it's on the verge of implosion. Lincoln Riley has spent the week answering questions about job security. I don't care who's lining up under center for Ryan Day, that's not exactly an inspiring sign of stability. North Carolina vs. No. 1 Miami Miami duo Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney combined for three touchdowns in the Hurricanes' win against Pitt in Week 8. (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill, North Carolina Line: Miami -14.5 Young: Miami The Hurricanes feel like 2025 Indiana. Litman: Miami The 'Canes keep rolling ahead of next week's massive showdown in South Bend against Notre Dame. Portnoy: Miami Short of Notre Dame next week, I'm not sure Miami won't win every game remaining on its schedule by at least two touchdowns. I'm buying stock in quarterback Darian Mensah as the eventual Heisman winner, and, for all the good UNC has done this year, it's not at the level of a national title contender like the Hurricanes. away.blurb: Georgia football was without KJ Bolden two weeks ago when they played Auburn. His status all week has been up in the air because he was marked questionable to play against Florida on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report. KJ Bolden's return might be exactly what Georgia needs Bolden's return to Georgia's lineup is coming at the perfect time. He originally suffered his injury against Alabama three weeks ago which is what led him to miss the Auburn game. Everyone knows how poorly that Auburn game went especially on defense as they didn't have an answer for Auburn's offensive strategy. Bolden however is making his return just in time for Georgia. The Bulldogs are about to embark on a critical stretch as they play three ranked opponents in row beginning with Florida on Saturday. Georgia is at their best when Bolden is starting on defense, so his return could be what propels UGA to get their season back on track. Georgia's injured 3-headed monster could all return in time to play Florida Georgia Bulldogs News: Florida QB controversy, Bulldog ruled out, new spread New reports on Friday however are indicating that he is expected to play against Florida on Saturday. Georgia football defensive back KJ Bolden injury update Bolden is a projected first round draft pick in next year's NFL Draft. Georgia has depth behind him that can step up and fill in, but no one can play at the same level as Bolden. The good news for Georgia is that he is expected to play against Florida on Saturday. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. (Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inside NU Archives · SB Nation Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:40 PM UTC · 10 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern has played itself into College Football Playoff contention. The 'Cats sit as the No. 20-ranked team in the nation, with six wins over South Dakota State, Colorado, Penn State, Michigan State, Ball State and Rutgers, and a narrow 29-23 loss on the road to the now No. 4-ranked Indiana Hoosiers. Thus far this season, they've passed the eye test, wowing pundits around the country with creative offensive formations and a turnover happy defense, but they are in need of quality wins over top-notch opponents. Over the next four weeks, NU will get three chances to secure resumé-changing victories, with matchups booked against Oregon, Iowa, Ohio State and Minnesota. The first of which, against Dan Lanning's Ducks, will take place on Saturday. Here's the INU staff's predictions for the 'Cats' road test against the 4-3 Oregon Ducks: Charlie Jacobs (27-16 Northwestern ) This Northwestern team has a different vibe to it. Although the Wildcats' last road trip was too close for comfort, Oregon has been struggling a lot lately and offers the perfect opportunity for Northwestern to pick up the win. Whether it's Brock Thomas or Dylan Raiola at quarterback, I'm not sure the Ducks can keep up with the Wildcats' offense, which will likely score enough no matter what. Plus, Chip Kelly back calling plays in Autzen… there's very few storylines better than that this week. Oregon, while a very talented roster, hasn't been able to put it all together. Even with a new offensive coordinator this week (or lack thereof), Oregon's offense has to prove it can compete for it to be threatening, even if the weapons are healthy. I'm taking the 'Cats. Jackson Pick (24-13 Northwestern ) Northwestern enters the meat of its schedule on a four-game winning streak, and at face value it's hard not to favor the 'Cats here. Aidan Chiles collected five total touchdowns against Rutgers on Saturday, with Caleb Komolafe adding one of his own to go with his 150 rushing yards on the day. Oregon, one of the preseason national championship favorites, has lost two of its last three, including a 21-10 shocker at Illinois that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. One reason for the Ducks' slide is obvious: their quarterback and potential No. 1-overall pick Dante Moore suffered a head injury against USC, and neither Dylan Raiola nor Brock Thomas have been able to sufficiently replace his production — Oregon has gone from 304 passing yards per game to just 205 since Moore's injury. On Saturday, Moore's continued absence will once again stifle an Oregon offense whose rushing attack hasn't produced enough to supplement its weakened passing game. While its defense has been stout enough, Northwestern will travel to Eugene with the strongest offense the Ducks have faced since their Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State. This game – if the Wildcats can win it – will begin to put the CFP in their sights. Autzen Stadium is a raucous environment to travel to for a NU team that's struggled on the road, and this is easily their biggest test since traveling to face Indiana. Unlike with the Hoosiers, though, the 'Cats don't need to execute at 100% to take this one. On another big day for the Wildcats' defense, Chiles will do just enough to escape Autzen with a season-defining victory. Donovan West (21-17 Oregon ) Five punts, three missed field goals and a fumble. That's how eight of Oregon's drives ended against Illinois last week. It was a masterclass in miscues from head coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks in a disappointing result that marked a season that has spun out of control. Despite a roster made up mostly of four- and five-star recruits, Oregon is 4-3 and has proven that raw talent doesn't automatically make a good football team. Northwestern, however, has proven the opposite. The 'Cats are an injury-ridden team of misfits that has united around a common goal and beaten the breaks off of three power conference teams. The only problem for NU is that its dominance has made the games boring to watch and has led to the Wildcat Wall leaving early.​ Yet, with the two programs on opposite trajectories, Oregon will still walk onto its home field on Saturday as favorites. The sports books trust the Ducks' depth and talent, and so do I. Their victories over USC and Nebraska, two wins more impressive than anything Northwestern has done, show that Oregon can still be a good football team. The Ducks will trot into Autzen Stadium knowing they need to win for any chance at making the playoff and grind their way to victory with a dominant performance in the trenches. As it did against Indiana, Northwestern will struggle to run the ball against Oregon, and Aidan Chiles won't be able to get it done through the air. The 'Cats' dreamy season will take a reality check, and expectations will be reevaluated. Zac Penson (24-17 Oregon ) I want to be wrong. The biggest hump I struggle to get over is that Oregon still has a stellar defense. Despite losing Dante Moore for the year, their experience and poise on defense is something they have continued to show over the past few weeks, allowing only 17 points to UCLA and just 14 points to Nebraska. Northwestern has also seemed to struggle on the road this season, falling to Indiana and squeaking out a win over Michigan State. And this stadium will be louder. Coming in at No. 20 on the AP Poll against an unranked Oregon team, the Wildcats have something to prove. Oregon lost to Illinois last week, so they clearly aren't invincible, but that was in Champaign. Autzen Stadium is a whole different animal. Despite losing to Illinois, Oregon is indeed favored. I would love to see the Cardiac 'Cats pull off the upset on this one, but I believe the pressure of the moment is only mounting for the Wildcats as the days drag on and they board their flight to Eugene. I believe Northwestern won't go down without a fight, though, and I expect this one to be a fun battle to the end. Whitley Williams (24-21 Northwestern ) Blurb: Strike while the opponent is weak. Northwestern is seeking its fifth consecutive win against the Oregon Ducks. Once considered a College Football Playoff contender, Oregon has endured a series of unexpected setbacks. The Ducks fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following their loss to Illinois. Once known for their explosive offense and "Pac-12 After Dark" spectacles, the Ducks are now a team searching for their identity. In many ways, the roles have reversed. Northwestern boasts a creative, explosive offense that keeps opposing defenses guessing. Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly will need to lean on that trickery against an elite Oregon defense that allows just 3.65 yards per carry and 197.6 passing yards a game. Assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson will call the plays for Oregon on Saturday. With Dante Moore out for the season, Oregon will start Dylan Raiola at quarterback. Against Illinois, Raiola completed 66% of his passes for 246 yards but couldn't finish the job. The Wildcats will have to lock down deep-threat wide receiver Dakorien Moore. Aidan Chiles has played extremely tough on the road in hostile environments, and this test in Eugene will certainly show what the Wildcats are truly made of. Kussh Mital (21-10 Northwestern ) I don't see why this game should be any different than Oregon's previous matchup against Illinois. I believe this so much that I am predicting that same score in the Wildcats favor. Oregon's defense is great, don't get me wrong, but they just gave up over 200 rushing yards to Illinois, and Northwestern has a flat out better rushing attack. Moreover, Northwestern can air the ball out much more efficiently, something the Ducks have not had to deal with in a couple weeks. Aidan Chiles is the best quarterback Oregon has faced since Jayden Maiava, who threw for over 300 yards and two touchdown passes against it. Chiles probably won't do that, but he will certainly do some damage. However, the main issue for this Oregon squad is the quarterback position. When you can't trust your quarterback to run the offense effectively, it's hard to expect to win the game. Even with the return of some of the receivers for Oregon, Dylan Raiola is not going to get the job done against Northwestern. With the Wildcats somehow entering the game as underdogs, I expect them to wear that title with honor and make Oregon fans extra fearful on Halloween. Drew Christmann (23-16 Northwestern ) Since Dante Moore went down with a scary and controversial injury against USC, Oregon has a simple problem: they can't score. Since that Week 4 matchup in LA, the Ducks have scored no more than 17 points a game, down from 47.5 in prior games, including an 84-0 shutout against Portland. Now, after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following a loss to Illinois last week, in which the Ducks scored just 10 points, it's unclear what Oregon's offense will look like going forward, with Dan Lanning confirming he doesn't expect Moore to return for the rest of the season. Northwestern is the opposite. After years of a less-than-optimal offense, the Wildcats have been one of the conference's best, especially on the ground, where they average 204.6 yards per game. Aidan Chiles has been no slouch in the air, too, throwing for 1,617 yards with a 71.3% completion rate and just one interception. That, along with Chip Kelly's return to Autzen, makes for a scary matchup for Oregon. The ideal situation for the 'Cats' is a quick start, as it did against Rutgers last week, when they scored on the first three possessions of the game. But Northwestern has shown they know how to play from behind in hostile environments, like in Bloomington, where they scored 16 points in the final quarter to push defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the brink and at Michigan State in East Lansing, where Chiles drove 64 yards against his former school to win on a game-winning kick. The Wildcats have shown they can win both ways, and against an Oregon team whose season is spiraling, I see Northwestern moving to 7-1 on Halloween. Adam Sutro (27-24 Northwestern ) I have low confidence in Northwestern's defense entering this football game. A poor Rutgers offense killed the 'Cats on the ground last week, exposing a run defense issue that has been a problem all year for Northwestern. Fortunately for the 'Cats, Oregon has operated more through the air than on the ground for most of the season… though I think with all the talent the Ducks have on their offensive line, they will figure out how to expose the 'Cats' run defense and move the ball. Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats
picks.blurb: That seems like a long time ago, doesn't it? Less than a week later, we are sitting with the Ducks at 4-3, having just fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following another loss, and quarterback Dante Moore announcing that his 2026 season is over after the concussion he suffered earlier this year against USC. Now, with a laundry list of questions to answer, the Ducks go forward into a brutal home matchup against the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats , hoping that they can somehow manage to get back to their winning ways. To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Question: Well, it's certainly been an eventful week in Eugene. Let's start with the biggest news: Dante Moore is not expected to play again this season. With the Ducks sitting at 4-3 and their playoff hopes essentially gone, what are your expectations for the rest of the season? What would a successful finish look like? Zachary Neel: At this point, a successful season is going 7-5 on the year and making it to a semi-respectable bowl game when all is said and done, and that's incredibly sad to say, considering where this season started. Just about everything has gone wrong for Oregon thus far, and I truly do see a reality where they struggle to even become bowl-eligible. But I think the culture wins out, and Dan Lanning can rally this team over the final five weeks. Bjorn Bergstrom: The culture that we’ve come to know in recent seasons is of a team that stays together and fights, no matter the circumstances. That hasn’t been the case in 2026, but if they can reclaim that fight and grittiness, then I think that should be considered a success. The way things are going, it’s hard to stamp “success” on a certain win total. It’s more about the process and the eye test, rather than the end result. Logan Brown: It’s hard to find any success in this season at this point. I guess if Oregon beats Washington, that’s probably the least you could ask for? I would say an 8-4 finish would mean the Ducks played well in November and finished strong, but that probably means losses to Northwestern and Ohio State. It’s probably going to get worse before it gets any better. Drew Mehringer Question: Dan Lanning made one of the biggest decisions of his coaching career on Sunday, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after Oregon's loss to Illinois. Do you agree with the decision, and how much of the blame for Oregon's offensive struggles falls on Mehringer compared to the players and other coaches? Zachary Neel: I think a change needed to be made, but I also don't think this change is going to lead to a switch being flipped for the Oregon offense. The problems go much deeper than just the play calling, in my opinion, and I don't think we're going to all of a sudden see the Ducks putting up 27-31 points per game because Mehringer is no longer in the building. As the OC, he was rightfully the guy to fall on the sword, but more changes are needed this offseason. Bjorn Bergstrom: It's hard not to agree with the decision. Fans had been on him from the very beginning, it seemed, but I was finally on board after last week’s debacle. As far as the blame, there’s some that goes to the position coaches who didn’t have their guys ready to play individually, but the play calls were what stuck out to me in particular. It didn’t seem like Mehringer had the ability to scheme up easy looks for his quarterbacks and easy running holes for his backs. There was a clear lack of creativity. Just watch any other top-25 team in college football and you’ll see the difference in outside-of-the-box thinking schematically that Mehringer just couldn’t manage to implement. Logan Brown: Unfortunately, I do feel like it was the right move. There were so many times where it just seemed like the offense was lacking situational awareness because of the play call. I lost count of the amount of times the Ducks ran a third down play, from any distance, where receivers were all running routes short of the sticks. There were zero aggressive calls, and more aiming and carefully crafting open receivers to the point where if the defense had an answer, there was no counter. I do think Oregon’s lack of offensive line and quarterback development has played a significant role in the offense’s struggles, but Mehringer was a clear issue that the Ducks could do something about midseason. New Play-Caller Question: Jay Johnson is taking over play-calling duties for the Ducks, and he'll have quite the challenge trying to turn this offense around. What's the biggest change you hope to see from Oregon's offense under Johnson? And realistically, how much improvement can we expect in just one week? Zachary Neel: Asking Johnson to come in and completely change this offense is unfair and unrealistic. I think at the best, you can hope that Oregon's offensive scheme looks more simplified, leaning more heavily on running between the tackles, finding a rhythm, and getting the ball past the sticks on down-and-distance situations. But as far as an entirely new scheme that looks different from what we've seen over the past seven weeks, I'm not expecting that. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest thing I’ll be wanting to see is more creativity in the passing game as far as Dylan Raiola’s platform, whether it be rolling him out, sprint-outs, or moving the pocket so it’s not a straight dropback. Moving the quarterback in the backfield makes it so much more difficult for a defense to pinpoint where he’ll be on a given play, opening up the run game at the same time as they’ll be just a step slower. Also, no more Wildcat. Yuck. Logan Brown: Take some chances! Oregon has nothing to lose at this point. The Ducks have Ferraris all over the offense, but most throws are horizontal or short of the sticks. Safeties play close to the line because the Ducks don’t trust their quarterback to air it out. At this point, the season is gone, so why not air it out? Why not run more counters and try to produce explosive plays on the ground? I don't think Johnson changes a ton in just one week, but I do think he could set the tone with a different plan on critical downs. Question: Northwestern comes to Eugene at 6-1, ranked No. 20 in the nation, with former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly running the offense. The Wildcats have been one of the biggest surprises in the Big Ten this season. What concerns you most about this matchup, and where do you think Northwestern has the biggest advantage over Oregon? Zachary Neel: Any time Oregon faces a true dual-threat quarterback who can beat you with his feet, Duck fans get worried. That has been the Achilles heel in Eugene for years, and Aidan Chiles is as good at that as anyone. With his ability both in the air and on the ground, plus Chip Kelly's offensive mind, I know that the Ducks' defense is going to have its hands full on Saturday. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think that Northwestern has a simple, yet very important advantage: they play sound, complementary football much, much better than the Ducks have this season. They’ve been a complete team, complimenting each other on offense, defense and special teams and picking up for the other when needed. That’s something Oregon hasn’t done this season, and I don’t expect them to on Saturday. Logan Brown: I’m so interested in this battle of the ground with Northwestern’s run game. They have a three-headed monster in the backfield, plus the mobility of quarterback Aidan Chiles. The Wildcats have run the ball so well this season, but it hasn’t always come easy on the road. Oregon has played the run better the past few weeks, but the Ducks couldn’t stop Illinois on the ground in the second half last week. If Northwestern runs the ball efficiently, they win with a huge advantage. If not, it can get interesting. Question: We've talked a lot about Oregon's offensive struggles, but the defense will have its hands full with Chip Kelly and a Northwestern offense that's been rolling this season. What's the biggest key for Oregon's defense to slow down the Wildcats and give the Ducks a chance to win? Zachary Neel: As I mentioned above, it's going to be all about slowing down the run for Northwestern. That means more than just Chiles, though. The Wildcats have a trio of very good running backs that can hurt you in different ways. If Northwestern is able to find success on the ground, it will open up the play-action passing game, where tight end Luke Dehnicke can be lethal. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest key is forcing Aidan Chiles to have an off day and revert back to his struggles from his first three seasons. During that time, Chiles was an erratic, turnover-prone passer lacking confidence. In 2026, he’s full of confidence and is an absolute baller, making plays that simply weren’t imaginable just 12 months ago. Getting in his face, making him feel pressure and not be able to get going with easy throws early is imperative for the Ducks. But with Kelly’s scheme, I lean towards Chiles being able to get going early. Logan Brown: I already talked about the run game, but the Ducks need to play disciplined against Chiles. The senior quarterback can burn them with RPO plays or just a regular read option. Northwestern utilizes the whole field with wide splits, so the pressure is on Oregon’s edge rushers more than ever to contain Chiles in the option and quick game and avoid getting caught too far up field. Gambling Corner Question: Gambling Corner: You get $100 to spread across the point spread (Oregon -3.5), and the Over/Under (47.5 points). How are you allocating your funds? Zachary Neel: Give me all $100 on Northwestern to cover. Vegas always knows something, but I don't know what in the world they've seen from the Ducks over the past month to consider them a 3.5-point favorite here. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think Northwestern will win, so I’m tempted to go there, but what in the world is pulling the over/under so high? Mehringer is gone but the bones of the offense are still here, along with a Ducks defense that has been dominant. I don’t see either team surpassing 24 points, so I’ll put all $100 on the under. Logan Brown: I’m putting $65 on Northwestern to cover the spread and the other $35 on the under. Northwestern’s offense is rolling right now, and Oregon’s is not, but I think both defenses could come to play on Saturday afternoon. Final Score Prediction Question: Who wins this game, and what is the final score? Zachary Neel: I've got Northwestern 27, Oregon 16. Bjorn Bergstrom: We’re about to see a Ducks team sitting at .500 as the calendar flips to November. Northwestern 20, Oregon 13. Logan Brown: Northwestern 24, Oregon 18. The Wildcats run the ball and grind the clock in the second half, and Oregon’s offense continues to struggle to find explosive plays. home.headline: Lanning: Matt Johnson and Dave Iuli Need Surgery as Oregon Releases First Northwestern Injury Report
home.blurb: Oregon will be thinner along both lines when ranked Northwestern visits Autzen Stadium on Saturday. Dan Lanning told reporters on Wednesday that defensive tackle Matt Johnson and right guard Dave Iuli are both headed for surgery, and neither has a timeline to return, according to Sports Illustrated's On SI Ducks coverage of the press conference. There was one piece of better news in the same answer. Freshman offensive lineman Immanuel Iheanacho, who sat out the 21-10 loss at Illinois, is practicing again. Iuli has started four games at right guard this season but has been out of the lineup for the last two, and he had been playing through the problem before that. Johnson is a reserve, yet an important one: he has been the first man off the bench behind starting tackles A'Mauri Washington and Bear Alexander, and he also missed the Illinois game. Losing both at once stings for a 4-3 team that is still sorting out its offense after a coordinator change and the news that Dante Moore is not expected back this season . Iheanacho's return would give the line a body back, but he is not guaranteed to be cleared by Saturday. The Big Ten requires four availability reports in game week, and the first one landed at 5 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday. It held no surprises, the Eugene Register-Guard noted , because every player ruled out had already been reported as hurt. home.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes host the Oregon Ducks on Saturday in Columbus. Before the season, this looked like a surefire top-10 battle in November. That’s not how things played out. The two teams have five losses between them, and Oregon owns three of those. With Davison out, Oregon will rely on Dierre Hill and Brandon Smith as its running back duo in Columbus. Hill has been productive with 399 rushing yards on 83 attempts. Smith has 207 rushing yards on 32 attempts. The Buckeyes have their own injury issues at running back with Ja'Kobi Jackson out. These are two teams that aren’t as healthy as they’d like to be heading into a game with this much on the line. Either way, losing Davison is a legit blow for the Ducks on Saturday. It helps Ohio State out slightly, but it doesn’t change the stakes for either side. Both programs need this one, and Saturday will be telling for where each team’s season goes from here. The Oregon Ducks got some tough injury news ahead of their Week 10 game against Ohio State on the road. The Ducks sit at No. 23 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and there’s a slim chance they end up in the field. Both Ohio State and Oregon are in must-win situations this weekend. Now the Ducks have taken another real injury hit ahead of the trip to Ohio Stadium. Oregon will be without RB Jordon Davison against Ohio State According to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Oregon will be without standout running back Jordon Davison against Ohio State due to a lower extremity injury. Zenitz noted the injury is considered short-term, meaning Davison could be back soon after Week 10 action. Still, it’s a massive loss for the Ducks. Oregon will be without its No. 1 running back while it’s already down starting quarterback Dante Moore. Moore’s absence forces Dylan Raiola to start for the Ducks once again on Saturday. Losing the top option in the backfield on top of that puts more pressure on Raiola in a tough road environment. Davison has 91 carries for 439 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. As a freshman in 2025, he ran for 667 yards and 15 touchdowns. He’s a huge part of what Oregon wants to do offensively, and the Ducks’ rushing attack will look different without him. Those three give Oregon a chance to make plays down the field even if the run game takes a step back. The Buckeyes’ secondary will need to be sharp to keep Raiola from finding a rhythm. home.blurb: Lanning said he and the coaching staff, including new play-caller Jay Johnson, made a checklist of risks they wanted to take if it was available to them. He mentioned they weren't going to take risks just to take more risks, but that they needed to get back to who they were. Lanning said the Ducks had several play calls dialed up, like a halfback pass that didn't work out, a reverse, and of course, a fourth-and-short on the goal line. Where in previous weeks, trailing by three with a chance to tie Lanning would have made the safer play, there was no doubt Oregon was going for it in the second half. "We were trying to designate a guy to be responsible for him and he can go either direction on a lot of plays," Lanning said. "So they have a big play action boot game and it’s tough when you’re not bringing edges for him not to just be able to break out of the pocket when they’re running those. So you like to bring edge pressure, but then there were moments where he’s going opposite the pressure and able to take that away. Smith turned heads in fall camp but was used sparingly in the first half of the season behind veteran sophomores Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. With both starters knocked out of the game with injury, Smith stepped up to the plate and delivered some explosive runs that had been missing in recent weeks. Smith rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown on just eight carries and caught another four passes for 32 yards out of the backfield. Oregon football coach Dan Lanning said all week that the Ducks had been uncharacteristically conservative amid three putrid offensive showings in the month of October. The fifth-year coach, who has very atypically punted on several fourth-and-short downs and called safe plays on third-and-long, citing that punting is sometimes better than any other alternative, had enough of that following a 21-10 loss to Illinois in Champaign . Halloween's 34-26 win over Northwestern was simply about "letting it hang." "We were playing not to lose and playing small ball and that’s not what we do," Lanning said of previous games. "We let it hang. That’s what I heard our players saying on the sideline all day: ‘We’re not playing small ball, let’s go.’" "Going into this game, we were going to be aggressive," quarterback Dylan Raiola said. "We’re not living in the past. We’re gonna worry about the present and the future." The Ducks converted on a short Brandon Smith run to take a lead they would never relinquish. home.blurb: EUGENE - The Oregon Ducks debuted at No. 23 in the first College Football Playoff rankings with three losses, and ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit is saying the quiet part out loud. A week after people were writing off Oregon’s season, the Ducks are still in the mix. "They find a way to beat a top 20 team in Northwestern. Now they got Ohio State on the road. I'm not saying they're going to win. I'm just saying if somehow, some way, they figure out a way to knock off Ohio State, Michigan, Michigan State, and Washington. I feel like there's a path," Herbstreit said. Still, Oregon’s chance to make a third consecutive playoff berth hinges on it winning out. The Ducks’ remaining games include Ohio State, the Michigan Wolverines, the Michigan State Spartans and the Washington Huskies. One way it could happen is if UCLA wins out, handing Illinois and USC another conference loss. Oregon would also want USC to beat No. 4 Indiana on Nov. 14 before losing to UCLA in the regular-season finale. So while it is partly out of Oregon's hands... the Ducks have a chance to help themselves on Saturday vs. Ohio State This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/oregon as Kirk Herbstreit Says The Quiet Part Out Loud About Oregon And The Playoff . The Ducks beat No. 20 USC 41-27 on the road and No. 25 Boise State 34-27 at Autzen Stadium. Their only loss to a team in the committee’s Top 25 was a 17-15 defeat to No. 8 UCLA. South Carolina vs Oklahoma Odds, Point Spread, Betting Lines South Carolina vs Oklahoma point spread : Oklahoma -3.5, South Carolina +3.5 South Carolina vs Oklahoma over/under : 44.5 Total Points South Carolina vs Oklahoma moneyline : South Carolina ML +138, Oklahoma ML -165 South Carolina is the hotter of the two teams, and it got there by turning the offense over to LaNorris Sellers and the run game. The Gamecocks opened the season with a 57-0 rout of Kent State, then hit a rough stretch with losses to Mississippi State , Alabama, and Kentucky , with the Alabama game their only SEC loss by more than one score. Since then, they've won back-to-back games over ranked opponents. On Oct. 10, they rolled No. 16 Florida 38-19, with Sellers accounting for five touchdowns, four through the air and one on the ground, and last Saturday they beat No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 on a walk-off 48-yard field goal. Sellers had three touchdowns in that one, throwing for 210 yards and carrying 18 times for 96 yards, and the Gamecocks came out of the gate fast, going 75 yards in 10 plays on their opening drive and then scoring again on a 31-yard Sellers run to take a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. The strength of this team is its ground game, which leads the SEC at 218.3 yards a game. Sellers has 507 rushing yards at 6.0 a carry and Matt Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns, so defenses are forced to account for two backfield threats before Sellers throws a pass. The weak spots are in the trenches and on defense. The offensive line has allowed 15 sacks and is missing Josiah Thompson, Dayne Arnett and Seth Smith, receiver Jayden Sellers is also done for the season, and edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah is out. Defensive back Quay'sheed Scott and running back Jawarn Howell are doubtful. The defense ranks 119th in success rate , allows 222.7 passing yards a game, and has just four interceptions, which is why South Carolina's games tend to be decided by whether the offense keeps scoring. One key note: Shane Beamer, who was an assistant head coach for the offense at Oklahoma under Lincoln Riley, knows this program well. Oklahoma has been a defense-first team that is still looking for a consistent offense. The Sooners opened with a 51-0 win over UTEP , then lost to Michigan, beat New Mexico, and fell to Georgia before pulling off the season's biggest upset, a 27-24 win over then-No. 1 Texas on October 10 in the Red River Rivalry. They followed that with a 21-13 loss to No. 15 Kentucky at home, a game they led 13-7 into the fourth quarter before Mateer threw two interceptions, one returned for a touchdown, and last Saturday they beat Mississippi State 23-15 on the road. That win was their best offensive day of the season, 467 total yards, with John Mateer completing 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns without a turnover and Isaiah Sategna catching eight passes for 164 yards, along with 184 rushing yards, well above their season average of 92.5. The identity is still their defense. Oklahoma ranks second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense, with 22 sacks, and it ranks second in adjusted EPA per play and success rate. The offense is the problem. The Sooners rank last in the SEC in total offense, have the conference's worst run game and sit 121st in offensive success rate, and they've scored fewer than 30 points in six straight games, every SEC game this season included. Mateer has 1,591 passing yards, a 66.7% completion rate, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions, and Sategna leads the receivers with 578 yards. Lastly, the injury list is long, with linebacker Taylor Heim, receiver Trell Harris, tight end Trynae Washington, cornerback Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje out; receiver Elijah Thomas doubtful; and Peyton and Eli Bowen and linemen Jake Maikkula and Fred Hinton questionable. The case for South Carolina in the first quarter starts with the price. At +106, the market is treating the first 15 minutes as close to a coin flip, while the full-game line has Oklahoma as a 4.5- to 5.5-point favorite and South Carolina's moneyline anywhere from about +150 to +175. That gap makes sense, because Oklahoma's advantages are the kind that build over four quarters: a defense that ranks near the top of the SEC and can grind an opponent down over four quarters. However, those advantages don't help much early in a game, and the early part of the game is exactly where South Carolina's offense has been at its best. The gap between the two offenses is the other piece. South Carolina has the SEC's top rushing attack, Oklahoma has the conference's worst run game and 121st-ranked success rate, and the Sooners have not been quick starters in their recent games. They trailed Kentucky 7-0 after the first quarter, and against Mississippi State their entire first-quarter output was a field goal. South Carolina, meanwhile, scored on both of its first two possessions against Tennessee and has a quarterback who can make a defense pay with one big play, as he did on the 31-yard run. Oklahoma's defense is excellent, but a Sellers-Fuller running game that forces it to defend the whole field is the kind of look that can produce a scripted score, and winning the quarter may only take one good drive. The weather may also tilt things toward the visitors. The forecast calls for rain on Saturday, most likely before kickoff, with a high near 65, and a damp field tends to favor the team that wants to run the ball. The Gamecocks also fell behind early in the Florida game before taking over, so a slow start is possible, but with a +106 price for what is likely a much closer first quarter than the full-game odds suggest, South Carolina is the better side. Pick: South Carolina 1Q ML (+106)

If the Sooners can continue their upward trajectory against the Gamecocks, they'll have a chance. If not - if John Mateer has to lead the team in rushing attempts and the Sooners average less than 4 yards per carry, then desperation will set in, Mateer will be forced to make plays - then bad things will happen. But if OU can run the ball just a little, Mateer can relax and guys like Isaiah Sategna and Rocky Beers and Lloyd Avant can help out the defense by moving the chains, changing the scoreboard and winning a home game. Final: Oklahoma 21, South Carolina 13 John Mateer found a healthy headspace in Starkville, but Saturday will be the first real test to see if he can stick to the plan. South Carolina's defense is not impenetrable, but it's a much better group than Mississippi State's, with difference-makers who can wreck drives and put Mateer into tough situations. It's likely there will be a turnover, and the test will be if OU's quarterback can rebound after that. History says he'll have a tough time. Brent Venables' defense will get its third look at talented quarterback LaNorris Sellers, but if Oklahoma is unable to finish off drives, the Gamecocks have shown they can notch dramatic victories. Final: South Carolina 20, Oklahoma 13 Someone from the future could tell me a plethora of different outcomes from Saturday's game, and I'd believe them. Oklahoma's offense certainly made progress against Mississippi State, and it's possible that the Sooners build on those improvements at home against South Carolina. But it also wouldn't be shocking if OU's offense regressed into the turnover-prone unit that it was against Kentucky, Georgia, New Mexico and Michigan. South Carolina comes into Norman on a two-game winning streak after ranked victories over Florida (on the road) and Tennessee - the Gamecocks seem like they're due for a letdown. While South Carolina's defense is better than Mississippi State's was, there are plenty of areas for the Sooners to expose, assuming they can play a similarly clean game on Saturday. Oklahoma needs a win to stay above .500, and I expect the Sooners to earn a close victory over the Gamecocks. Final: Oklahoma 20, South Carolina 17 The Gamecocks are more dangerous than Mississippi State, on both sides of the ball. Last week was a small step forward for the Sooners' offense, nota giant leap. Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't completely fixed just because he had a solid game against the Bulldogs. But with Michael Fasusi back on the offensive line, the Sooners' offense adds layers. They don't have to have every element working in order to be successful. What they do need to do, though, is protect the football and keep up their strong defensive play. This game will be back and forth and figures to go down to the wire, but in the end, Oklahoma does just enough to start its first winning streak of the season. Brady Trantham The 2026 season is still up in the air. One thing it has told us is that basically no one has been able to handle a big emotional win and follow that up with another win a week later. South Carolina's win over Tennessee was very much an emotional win against a highly-ranked opponent - the Volunteers themselves had just beaten Alabama the week prior. OU has slowly built consistency on offense, just enough that paired with an elite defense, victories against flawed teams are realistic. The Sooners have proven to be great at corralling mobile quarterbacks and will showcase that again, while John Mateer will build off a great performance last week against a dangerous but very gettable defense. Can a South Carolina team with three SEC losses get to the College Football Playoff? If it closes with seven straight wins – including last week's victory over Tennessee and a win in late November against Georgia – it's not totally off the table. Can an Oklahoma team with three losses get to the College Football Playoff? If it closes with five straight wins – including the win over Texas a few weeks ago and if it picks up November wins over Florida, Ole Miss, and Missouri – it's not totally off the table. But the loser of this is definitely out – the CFP won't take a four-loss at-large team. The winner survives, advances, and can keep the dream alive. South Carolina vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes to Florida next, but this starts a run of three of the next four games at home. South Carolina hosts Texas A&M next before going to Arkansas. It closes with Georgia and at Clemson. It's only the third meeting between the two. Oklahoma won 26-7 last year, but South Carolina won 35-9 in 2024. It's not like it's going out there with no more fudge (this is a family show) to give after losing three straight, but it's been loose, relatively relaxed, and it's balling out with strong wins over Florida and Tennessee. The turnovers slowed to a crawl after giving it away twice in four straight games – there was just one interception against Tennessee in the last two – and the defense has done its part with three takeaways against Florida and one against the Vols. Why Oklahoma Will Win Oklahoma is still cranking up the defense, but it's just about the scoring. Sometimes the Sooners have to manufacture points from other areas – like they did against Texas – and that's where the defense has to come up large. The D doesn't have to score, but it needs to force South Carolina to start screwing up again. Oklahoma has come up with takeaways four times, with two in each game. It's 3-1 when it forces mistakes, because that leads to easy points for a team that's struggling to get the offense consistently moving. You want to get even sillier? Okay, let's go. In a never-screw-with-a-streak sort of way, Oklahoma has alternated win-loss-win-loss from the start, and if the pattern holds, it's due for a loss. To rein this in, South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers is playing well at just the right time. He might not be going crazy, but he's making plays, keeping things moving, and he's playing like a quarterback who can win games. The four-touchdown pass win at Florida showed what he could do on the road. In this, he'll have to make one or two big plays late. As he showed against Tennessee, he can do that. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. South Carolina: Initial injury report for Week 9
home.blurb: On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotation linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton Bowen's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.headline: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma injury report: Jawarn Howell, Quay'Sheed Scott ruled out
home.blurb: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma injury report: Jawarn Howell, Quay'Sheed Scott ruled out Skip to main content About On Thursday evening, just two days before the Gamecocks are set to kick off, South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer announced that Gamecock running back Jawarn Howell and defensive back Quay'Sheed Scott will both be out for Saturday's game. Coach Beamer gave the update during his weekly radio show, stating that both guys will be out for the game against the Sooners. “It will say that ‘Sheed is out again this week,” Beamer said via Gamecock Central . “He’s got some tests that have to get done tomorrow, and we’re optimistic on what those test will say, and if they say what we hope it’s going to say, he’ll be playing next week against Texas A&M. Jawarn won’t play Saturday; he banged his shoulder up, I guess Wednesday, in practice last week or maybe it was Friday, but late in the week. He was available last week in the Tennessee game, just has still been bothering him, and we thought the best thing for him was just still to be able to rest that shoulder a little bit this week and get that healthy. So those two are out.” Scott has not played since South Carolina's Oct. 3 game at home against the Kentucky Wildcats. The Gamecocks starting nickelback left the game and did not return, even having to be hospitalized as a precaution. Coach Beamer has not disclosed the specifics regarding his injury. Howell has also missed time this season with an injury, as he did not play in last week's win over Tennessee. Although his status changed from doubtful to questionable throughout the week last week ahead of the game against the Vols, he was ruled out and did not play. South Carolina Football All-Time LIsts South Carolina Football Recruiting South Carolina Basketball All-Time Lists South Carolina Basketball Recruiting The South Carolina Gamecocks will be without two players as the team seeks a third-straight victory over Oklahoma on Saturday. The running back has been a nice complement to South Carolina's backfield, led by Jabree Coleman and Matt Fuller. Through four games, Howell has rushed for 104 yards on 18 carries, averaging 5.8 yards per rush. Scott has nine total tackles with three passes defended so far this season. South Carolina will have a tough task going on the road against Oklahoma. The Sooners have notched victories over Texas and Mississippi State this season, and have the same record as South Carolina at 4-3. The Gamecocks are listed as 3.5-point road underdogs . picks.headline: Advanced Analytics Predict Clemson vs. Florida State
picks.blurb: Advanced Analytics Predict Clemson vs. Florida State Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Every year, the Clemson Tigers meet the Florida State Seminoles in ACC play in what is an annual rivalry in the conference. In 2026, it happens to fall on Halloween. The Tigers are looking to bounce back from a loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies last weekend, falling to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. Now, head coach Dabo Swinney enters a hostile environment at Doak Campbell Stadium, looking to turn it around. However, the advanced analytics say otherwise. Versus Sports Simulator predicts the Tigers will lose by double digits, which would be the third time this season that they do so if the score is replicated. The model has Florida State winning by a score of 30-20, giving the Seminoles a 71% chance to win on Saturday. Since Clemson has begun to slip in games, the Tigers’ chance to win this game has dropped. Going into the season, Swinney’s group had a 45% chance to win at Tallahassee, but the offensive struggles throughout the season have seen those odds plummet. The lowest it got for the Tigers was after the loss to Miami, only holding a 22% chance. While Versus grades Clemson’s defense at a B grade, the Tigers’ C+ offense is what sets them back in this game. Meanwhile, Florida State’s offense is graded at a B+, led by dual-threat quarterback Ashton Daniels, and the plethora of weapons around him on the Seminole offense. It’s also important to note that this game has only been picked wrong once by the model, which was last year in Clemson’s home win. Otherwise, the advanced analytics typically follow how the game goes in terms of picking a winner. The game script is simple for Swinney: his offense has to play better, especially through the air. The glaring issue is that Clemson has only two passing touchdowns on the year, which is the fewest in the FBS in its seven games played this season. If the Tigers can get a score through the air, or even pick up first downs from throwing the football, they will have a shot at taking down the Seminoles in their own building yet again. However, we have yet to see that often thus far. Especially in an away environment, Clemson will have to be sound on both sides of the football, maybe even winning the turnover margin, to win as an underdog on Saturday night. If not, it could end up being a trick instead of a treat on the gridiron. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m., and the game will be broadcast on the ACC Network. picks.headline: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s massive road matchup vs Florida State
picks.blurb: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s massive road matchup vs Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Staff score predictions for Clemson’s massive road matchup vs Florida State Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Clemson and Florida State have both fallen well short of expectations this season, but Saturday night's matchup in Tallahassee still carries plenty of intrigue as the longtime ACC rivals look to get things back on track. The Tigers (4-3, 2-2 ACC) are hitting the road for the first time in more than a month, looking to bounce back from a frustrating 20-16 loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson appeared to be in position to secure another conference victory before the Hokies scored the go-ahead touchdown in the final two minutes. True freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds continues to gain valuable experience, but Clemson's offense has struggled to find consistency. Reynolds completed 20 of 26 passes for 153 yards against Virginia Tech, although four sacks made things difficult for the young signal-caller. Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) enters the matchup coming off a bye week, giving the Seminoles extra time to prepare. Before the break, FSU pushed No. 1 Miami to double overtime in a 43-35 loss, with quarterback Ashton Daniels accounting for five touchdowns. Recent history favors Clemson, which has won nine of its last 10 meetings with Florida State. However, with both programs searching for answers, neither team can afford to take anything for granted. Saturday's contest kicks off at 7 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium, with ACC Network carrying the broadcast. Can Clemson continue its recent success against the Seminoles, or will Florida State defend its home field? Here's how our staff sees Saturday night's matchup playing out. Alex Turri: Clemson 17, Florida State 21 Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney talks with Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds (2) after he threw a ball out of bounds during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium Saturday, October 24, 2026. While Florida State's defense has been one of the worst in college football this season, Clemson's offense is doing the same thing. For me, this game comes down to which unit can step up and played just a little better than their norm. Unfortunately, I think the Seminoles' defense is more likely to rise to the occasion. You need to be able to throw the ball in college football to truly succeed, and Clemson just can't do it. Road loss for Dabo Swinney and the Tigers. Steve Holley: Clemson 19, Florida State 23 Clemson's offense hasn't been able to find the end zone more than once in either of its last two ACC games. Florida State has given up plenty of yards -- 434.9 per game this season, which ranks eighth from last in all of FBS. It's hard for me at this point to trust this Clemson offense for long drives that end in six points. Expect a close and competitive game like most Clemson-FSU matchups, but simply put: I trust FSU's bottom-of-the-barrel defense more than Clemson's bottom-of-the-barrel offense. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. FSU loses double-overtime heartbreaker to Miami Social media reactions to the end of FSU vs. Miami Column: ACC replay review never entertained another outcome on FSU’s final play FSU running back Ousmane Kromah carted off near the end of first half against Miami Despite having a losing season record, FSU’s offense is ranked T-49th in the nation in total offense, 50th in scoring, 46th in rushing, 63rd in passing, and 34th in red-zone offense. FSU individual leaders After allowing Miami to rack up 583 total yards on 78 plays for a 7.5 yard average/play, FSU’s defense now ranks 130th in the nation, giving up 435 yards/game, 124th in passing defense (256 yards/game), T-112th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert nearly 43% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-104th in first-down defense, allowing their opponents 155 first downs (22.1/game) in the 7 games played this season. I do not think Clemson is a good football team. However, they probably have the best unit on the field: their defense. Another issue for Florida State is that the Seminoles have historically struggled against the Tigers, with no home wins in the last decade. Even so, FSU should win on Saturday night. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game.
