FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. picks.blurb: Clemson Tigers final odds and prediction for Week 9 at Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball and softball FanSided NCAA Sites Clemson has been left with no choice but to pick up the pieces after last week's soul-crushing loss to Virginia Tech. It may have only counted as one defeat on the ledger, but it really did feel like 2.5 losses mentally. For better or worse, the Tigers must turn the page and get ready for potentially a wild road game at the rival Florida State Seminoles. It will be during Halloween, nevertheless, so get ready for it. Clemson enters play at 4-3 on the season and 2-2 in the ACC. It has wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, with losses to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech. While Florida State is only 3-4 on the season, Mike Norvell's Seminoles have a knack for scoring points and playing some fairly competitive football at home. Dabo Swinney cannot let his team overlook FSU. With that all in mind, here are the latest betting odds, how to watch this game, and a game prediction. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Florida State will be laying 5.5 points to visiting Clemson. The associated moneylines for this game are Florida State -215 and Clemson +180. This means that it would take a $215 bet on Florida State to win $100, while wagering $100 on Clemson would pocket you $180. The projected point total for the game comes in at a combined 49.5 points, down from 51.5. Using all of that information above, a projected final score for this game would be something in the vicinity of Florida State 27.5, Clemson 22. While the odds for this game have fluctuated a bit , Florida State has been the favorite throughout for two reasons. It is a home game for the Seminoles, and the meager Tigers' offense has struggled to score points against Power Four competition all season long. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. How to watch Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles Here is what you need to know to be able to watch Clemson take on Florida State on Halloween night. Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:00 p.m. ET Location: Tallahassee, FL Venue: Doak Campbell Stadium TV Info: ACCN Streaming Info: fuboTV Radio: 105.5 FM (The Roar)/Clemson Athletic Network Kickoff from Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, FL, will be at 7:00 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. The ACC Network will carry the conference rivalry game. You can stream the game on fuboTV. You can listen to the game over the airwaves on 105.5 FM The Roar, or you can check out any other radio affiliates on the Clemson Athletic Network. You are not going to want to miss this rivalry game! Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles game prediction This high-stakes ACC rivalry game will come down to one of two things. From the Florida State perspective, it will be all about how disciplined the Seminoles' pass defense will be. This team can score points, but it does love to give them up in bunches. As for Clemson, the Tigers need to show on offense that they can put up 30 or so points if they need to get into some sort of a low-end shootout. Right now, it is so hard to fathom Clemson getting into the end zone at least three times on Saturday. The Tigers are going to need three touchdowns, and presumably 12 points from Nolan Hauser on special teams, to realistically have a chance at pulling off the upset. Gideon Davidson may get one on the ground, possibly two if he gets lucky. This will come down to whether Tait Reynolds can throw for one. Unfortunately, Clemson's offense is not built right now to score quickly and in bunches, so it will lose. Week 9 final score prediction: Florida State 30, Clemson 24. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. The game can be seen on ACC Network. Wes Durham and Max Browne will have the call of the game. Madison Fitzpatrick will report from the sidelines. The Clemson Athletic Network feed of the game featuring Tigers radio play-by-play voice Don Munson and analysts Tim Bourret and Jeff Scott can be heard on SiriusXM channel 258. By Michael Schwartz in College Football Published: October 31, 2026 at 3:56 pm EDT Clemson visits Tallahassee for a Halloween night ACC showdown Red-zone finishing and run defense headline this Saturday night matchup Read below for my Clemson vs Florida State prediction and picks As the Clemson Tigers (4-3) hit the road to face the Florida State Seminoles (3-4), both teams find themselves desperate for a bounce-back victory. Florida State enters this ACC clash fresh off an Oct. 24 bye week following a hard-fought 43-35 defeat against Miami, while the Tigers recently stumbled in a tight 20-16 home loss to Virginia Tech. With both squads going 1-2 over their last three outings, finding a rhythm before November is paramount. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET this evening under the lights at Bobby Bowden Field at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida. The home squad will look to lean on its passing attack to defend its turf, while the visiting Tigers must rely on their stingy defense to grind out a road upset. In this preview, we break down both teams' recent form, highlight the key statistical mismatches and outline our Clemson vs Florida State picks for this Saturday night showdown, using the current college football odds as a starting point. Clemson vs Florida State Prediction Clemson vs Florida State prediction: Florida State covers at home in a game that clears 51.5 points. Florida State's offensive production dwarfs Clemson's sluggish attack. The Seminoles score touchdowns on 75% of their red-zone trips (21 of 28), while the Tigers sit at 39.1% (9 of 23). Clemson's defense is the best unit in this game, allowing just 21.3 points and 317.0 yards per game, but its offense has given it little support. Clemson vs Florida State Picks Clemson vs Florida State Pick #1: Florida State -6.5 Pick: Florida State -6.5 (50¢ on Polymarket) Florida State enters this matchup possessing a substantially more potent offense. The Seminoles are racking up 31.6 points and 414.3 total yards per game, easily outpacing Clemson's 21.4 points and 333.1 yards per contest. A critical differentiator in this game will be third-down efficiency; Florida State extends drives at a 41.8% clip, while the Tigers move the chains at just 31.7%. Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels is a true dual threat. He has amassed 1,618 passing yards and 12 passing touchdowns against eight interceptions, while adding 354 rushing yards and 11 scores on the ground. Contrast this with Clemson's Tait Reynolds, who has thrown for 1,096 yards with one touchdown against three interceptions this season. At 50¢, the spread is priced as a coin flip. Given their superior scoring ability and red-zone finishing, the Seminoles have the firepower to cover this number. Clemson vs Florida State Pick #2: Over 51.5 Pick: Over 51.5 (48¢ on Polymarket) Florida State's offense is high-scoring, but its defense is generous, surrendering 434.9 total yards and 27.9 points per game. Over their last three games, the Seminoles' run defense has regressed, allowing 230.3 rushing yards per contest. Clemson running back Gideon Davidson (492 rushing yards, five touchdowns) should find room to exploit that vulnerability. Combining the two teams' season scoring averages puts this game right around 53 total points, above the 51.5 line. Both teams also carry a -4 turnover margin, and short fields created by giveaways can lead to quick points. At 48¢, the Over implies a 48% chance of cashing. Florida State's scoring and its defensive problems make that the side I prefer. Clemson vs Florida State Saturday Night Odds Florida State +6.5 (52¢) -6.5 (50¢) Over 51.5 (48¢) Under 51.5 (54¢) Current Polymarket buy prices establish Florida State as a clear home favorite, with its moneyline at 68¢ against 34¢ for Clemson. The spread is close to a dead heat, with Florida State -6.5 at 50¢ and Clemson +6.5 at 52¢. On the total, the Under (54¢) is priced above the Over (48¢), so the market leans slightly toward a lower-scoring game. TALLAHASSEE, FL — Clemson football starting left guard Elyjah Thurmon was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital on Nov. 1 after being carted off vs. Florida State the day before, according to the school. "OL Elyjah Thurmon has been discharged from the hospital and is returning to Clemson ," Clemson football's X account posted. home.headline: Clemson’s Elyjah Thurmon carted off field after suffering serious injury vs. Florida State
home.blurb: Clemson’s Elyjah Thurmon carted off field after suffering serious injury vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery What MLB's labor proposal means Brad Taningco, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sun, November 1, 2026 at 2:28 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Dabo Swinney and the Clemson Tigers are hoping to make up for their disappointing loss to Virginia Tech against Florida State. However, both teams took a moment to think about something other than the game after offensive lineman Elyjah Thurmon suffered a serious head-to-head collision. Clemson's entire team went onto the field in concern for their teammate, while Florida State players also took a knee as Thurmon was getting treatment. Thurmon was eventually carted off the field , and he was able to raise his right hand to give a thumbs up to the applauding crowd. The offensive lineman was trying to block during a running play early in the second quarter. But as several players converged onto the ball, he was hit in the head and was unable to get back up. Thurmon is in his third year at Clemson. After appearing in 11 games in his first two season, he has featured in seven of the team's first eight games. Despite the concern of seeing one of their teammates carted off with a serious injury, Clemson was able to rally and take a 23-10 lead into halftime. They scored 13 points in a row after Thurmon's injury thanks to two field goals and a Tait Reynolds touchdown pass to Olsen Patt-Henry. Like Florida State, Clemson is desperate to pick up the win amid a disappointing season thus far. Apart from a victory against North Carolina, they don't have any other quality wins to speak of. Nevertheless, Dabo Swinney will be looking to finish the season strong and hopefully get more recruiting wins in the process. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Miami looks to stay unbeaten against a sneaky-good North Carolina team on the road Getty Images Prior to last week, Miami had not held the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 poll since 2002, but so far the Hurricanes are looking every bit the part of the best team in the country. Not only have they raced out to a 7-0 start this year, but they've done so in a way that suggests a continuation of the success that led Miami all the way to the national championship game last season. With a 14-1 record in its last 15 games, Miami has been one of the best teams in the country since early November 2025, and now each week provides yet another opportunity for this year's team to validate that high poll ranking. This week, that means a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina in a game that offers Cristobal and Miami a chance to reverse a recent skid in the series. The Tar Heels have won their last five meetings in the series, including a 2-0 record against Cristobal with wins in 2022 and 2023. But those two Miami teams finished a combined 12-13 overall, while this year's group is clearly playing on a different level. For starters, those teams didn't have not just one but two Heisman Trophy contenders like Miami does this year with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney . Those last teams that lost to North Carolina also didn't carry the nation's best scoring margin, as Miami does currently, beating opponents by 33.7 points per game. There's some history that favors UNC, sure, but Miami's strength will challenge the impact of the past. Miami vs. North Carolina: Need to know Tar Heels looking to bounce back from upset home loss: While Miami validated its position at No. 1 last week with a thorough thrashing of Pitt, North Carolina saw some of the hype for this matchup cooled by an upset loss at home to Syracuse . The Tar Heels led by 10 points in the fourth quarter but let Steve Angeli and the Orange offense back into the game with a couple late scores before eventually falling in overtime. That's brought even more urgency to Bill Belichick's crew to have their game locked in for Saturday night, because the kind of failure at the margins that led to the fourth-quarter collapse will only be exposed more dramatically against a team of Miami's caliber. The Tar Heels have shown in wins over TCU , Pitt and Duke that they can play a tight game and come out on the right side of close margins, but those victories (and certainly any upset effort against Miami) require a cleaner effort than North Carolina showed against Syracuse last week. A Saturday showcase spot for Miami's Heisman Trophy contenders: Miami has a nice two-week run where its opponents and the stage will allow for quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney to receive a big-time spotlight in the national conversation. This week's game against North Carolina, on Halloween night in Chapel Hill, will draw plenty of attention and could allow the Hurricanes (who are 14-point favorites) to continue building the resumes of both Mensah and Toney. Mensah is putting together one of the best starts to a season we have seen from a quarterback this century, currently leading the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) while also rolling up 22 passing touchdowns (2nd in FBS) and 307.3 passing yards per game (fourth in FBS). Malachi Toney, meanwhile, leads the FBS in receptions (66) and has become the first wide receiver with at least 900 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns on a 7-0 team since eventual Heisman winner DeVonta Smith in 2020. Miami is elite in the middle (of games): It's easy to look at the collection of talent Mario Cristobal has assembled as an explanation for the team's dominance, but that talent has to perform to deliver the kind of results the Hurricanes have been getting over the last two seasons. Part of winning big has been winning small, and for Miami that's included dominating the middle portions of games. The Hurricanes have the No. 1 point differential in the second quarter in all of FBS (+95) and No. 3 point differential in the third quarter (+57). Miami is also No. 3 nationally this season in "middle 8" scoring (the last four minutes of the second quarter and the first four minutes of the third quarter), with a +7.6-point average on the season. The Hurricanes, ranked No. 4 at the time, were 6-0 and looking to establish themselves as the class of the ACC, having joined the conference just a few years removed from a national championship. A lot has been made about Miami's struggles in the last five meetings, but the Hurricanes' issues with the Heels date back to the very beginning of their time in the league, and Connor Barth's game-winning kick to seal the spooky upset. Bill Belichick and North Carolina's defense can get enough stops to keep this close, and with Notre Dame on deck, the Hurricanes might not be in the mindset to push this game deep into the evening. We're projecting North Carolina to flirt with the cover, but ultimately for the total to come in under the oddsmaker's number. UNC Tar Heels Preview, Injury Report, and Extra - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery TRENDING First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre · Roundtable Sports Sat, October 31, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Raleigh (NC). – The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes will face the North Carolina Tar Heels on Saturday for a spooky Halloween prime-time night. Here's all there is to know heading into the Atlantic Coast Conference clash at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill (NC): Television Channel: ABC Kickoff Time: 7:30 p.m. E.T. The Hurricanes are -750 favorites to win; meanwhile, the Tar Heels receive a +475 chance of pulling off a major upset. The spread is currently at 13.5 and the over/under at 53.5. According to the ACC availability report, the Hurricanes are relatively healthy, as the usual six are ruled out: wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-Body; Out for Season), running back CharMar "Marty" Brown (Right Knee; Out for Season), cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left Knee), cornerback Romanas "OJ" Frederique Jr. (Left Shoulder), tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season). Tar Heels starting cornerback Tre Miller (undisclosed) is ruled out for Saturday's game. He hasn't played since UNC's 21-17 upset over No. 25 Pitt on Oct. 10. A few other starters' statuses are currently uncertain. Safety Peyton Waters (undisclosed) is listed as questionable and hasn't played since the Tar Heels' 24-20 win over Duke on Oct. 17, missing last Saturday's 31-30 loss to Syracuse. Left tackle Jordan Hall (undisclosed) is listed as questionable and has only played in four games this season. Left guard Andrew Threatt (undisclosed) is listed as questionable and only played 30 snaps against Syracuse. In other related news, defensive end Zavion Griffin-Haynes (undisclosed) is completely off the injury report. He was initially listed as questionable. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Viliami Moala, wide receiver Keeyun Chapman, defensive tackle Vodney Cleveland, and defensive tackle Jimmy-Phrisco Alo-Suliafu are ruled out. The Hurricanes' interior offensive line will be challenged by UNC's defensive tackle Xavier Lewis, who is second in the ACC with seven sacks. After allowing a season-high 14 pressures in last Saturday's 52-23 win over Pitt, the unit will need to tighten up, as quarterback Darian Mensah continues to lead the Football Bowl Subdivision with an 81.4 completion percentage. As the Tar Heels have the fourth-worst passing offense in the ACC, it's an opportunity for the Hurricanes' secondary to limit explosive plays. The unit has allowed a combined 17 between Pitt and Florida State. The Hurricanes will look to overcome past struggles at Chapel Hill. away.blurb: Miami star wide receiver Malachi Toney is expected to undergo ankle surgery following an injury sustained in practice on Wednesday, according to a report from CBS Sports which noted the injury is not expected to be season-ending. ESPN first reported the injury, adding that the surgery is for a high-ankle sprain and will likely keep him out at least four weeks, starting with Saturday’s marquee game at No. 11 Notre Dame. That points to Toney missing the remainder of the regular season but potentially being available for the College Football Playoff should the Hurricanes qualify. If Toney is unable to play against the Fighting Irish, Miami’s options to fill in as the starting slot receiver would most likely be sophomore Daylyn Upshaw (who has been starting alongside Cooper Barkate as an outside receiver) and true freshman Vance Spafford. Moving Upshaw to the slot would open the door for South Carolina transfer Vandrevius Jacobs or true freshman Somorian Wingo, both of whom are threats in the deep passing game but have seen limited playing time this season, to start on the outside with Barkate. The top-ranked Miami Hurricanes look like they’ll be without their most dynamic player in their most highly anticipated game of the regular season and beyond. “Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday’s practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team’s medical staff,” the school said in a statement Wednesday afternoon. “We will share additional updates as appropriate.” Toney ranks second nationally with 73 catches, third with 1,027 receiving yards and tied for second with 13 touchdown receptions. He has recorded double-digit catches in four of eight games and has eclipsed 100 receiving yards in five of eight contests, including going for 234 yards and three touchdowns in Miami’s season-opener against Stanford, 154 yards and two touchdowns in a double-overtime win against Florida State and 194 yards and three touchdowns two weeks ago against Pittsburgh. He is one of the frontrunners for the Heisman Trophy, along with his quarterback Darian Mensah. Toney has not missed a game in his college career but has briefly left a few games this season with apparent injuries before promptly returning. Barkate is second on the team with 28 catches, 372 yards and four catching touchdowns. Upshaw has 22 catches, 263 yards and two touchdowns. Tight end Elija Lofton has 20 catches, 236 yards and two touchdowns. Toney already holds the school records for catches in a game (16, set Oct. 24 against Pittsburgh), receiving yards in a game (234, set Sept. 4 against Stanford), receiving yards in a season (1,211 in 2025) and receptions in a season (109 in 2025) while being tied for receiving touchdowns in a game (three, done twice by him this season and matching the mark done five other times in school history) and in a season (13 this year, matching Leonard Hankerson’s mark from the 2010 season). home.blurb: North Carolina had the football back with just under seven minutes in the fourth quarter, needing a touchdown to re-take a lead once-again, but the Hurricanes delivered with a strip-sack and sucked all the life out of Tar Heel Nation. Miami scored a touchdown on its ensuing drive, with Heisman Trophy candidates Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney connecting for their second scoring of the night and UNC's Halloween magic ran out , losing 38-35. North Carolina (4-4, 2-3 ACC) made things interesting late again with 1:38 left in the final quarter, as Edwards and former Wisconsin teammate Trech Kekahuna connected on a 15-yard slant. The Tar Heels then recovered consecutive onside kicks, only for penalties to wipe those out. The Hurricanes recovered UNC's third and final onside kick attempt, running the clock out to survive a scare from the boys in Carolina Blue. Miami won an offensive shootout with 422 yards, as Mensah, Toney and Mark Fletcher each scored twice. Approximately 90 minutes before kickoff, the Tar Heels ruled starting safety Peyton Waters and reserve linebacker Jonathan Agumadu out for tonight's ACC battle vs. top-ranked Miami. It's Halloween, after all, which means plenty of trick-or-treating. On UNC's walk over to Kenan Stadium, head coach Bill Belichick and his players handed out candy to fans. Jelani Thurman caught virtually every pass thrown to him, including Edwards' first two scoring strikes. North Carolina wanted the win more than anything, but should be proud of scaring the Hurricanes. Since Sayin went down, Ohio State on SI (and I included) have done our best to bring Buckeye Nation as many perspectives as possible as the season resumes Saturday night in Los Angeles against the USC Trojans. Given the parity in this year's wacky college football season, the Buckeyes have yet to have a true reality-check moment. This week isn’t it either. The Badgers, who play the Iowa Hawkeyes earlier in the day’s action, suffocated the Trojans in all areas last week in Madison in one of the sport’s most shocking upsets. Although Halloween night could call for a spooky outcome (pun purposely intended), it’s hard to pick against Ohio State in Big Ten play, regardless of who the quarterback ends up being, until it loses in league play. So far, I’m the lone undefeated picker this season, so riding the hot hand with coach Ryan Day’s team against a depleted Trojans bunch seems like a smart pick (although all-time series history says otherwise). Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 24, USC 14 Ohio State has reached the crux of its season, not necessarily because of where they stand in Big Ten competition at this point in its schedule, but because we don’t know for sure what the Buckeyes will look like without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future. Not to take anything away from the 6-2 Trojans, but what was originally supposed to be a road game against a solid-but-not-elite conference opponent has now shifted its focus entirely on how the Buckeyes will look with a freshman starting at quarterback, be it true freshman Luke Fahey or redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. Having said that, Ohio State still wields a deeper and more talented roster overall, headlined by the best player in the game, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes’ staff has more than enough resources to work with to keep whichever quarterback ends up starting well protected scheme-wise. Look for a lot of quick passes and screens on offense, while the defense figures out a way to pressure Jayden Maiava into committing mistakes, just like Wisconsin did last week. With the Buckeyes being favored by a touchdown on the spread (-7), I’m picking them to cover thanks to another solid performance on defense. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 24, USC 21 The Wisconsin Badgers’ 24-7 win over USC last Saturday has Ohio State fans understandably wondering whether the Buckeyes will follow a comparable game plan. I am guessing that Luke Fahey will be the starting quarterback, and that the coaching staff has emphasized to Fahey to play efficiently in a style reminiscent of when Julian Sayin made his first start at home vs. Texas in 2025. The USC defensive line has the pass rushing ability to get after an opposing quarterback, and I believe Fahey will use his legs to get out of the pocket and make positive yards to keep drives alive. Ohio State's defense is going to be tested all game against a formidable USC offense, despite the issues that the Trojans had last week in Madison. Maybe it's wishful thinking on my part, but this game has some serious Tresselball vibes for me going into Saturday night against an USC team that has its back to the wall. Yards and points may be difficult for the Buckeyes to earn, but I believe the Buckeyes will exhale when Connor Hawkins makes a late field goal in the final minutes of the contest. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, USC 14 For the first time during Ryan Day’s tenure as Ohio State head coach, a backup quarterback will start for the Buckeyes in a Big Ten matchup. It is still unknown if that starter will be true freshman Luke Fahey, or former 5-star sophomore Tavien St. Clair. Although, what is known coming into this matchup is that the USC defense has been one of the worst defenses against the pass in the Big Ten this season. Learning curves should be there for whatever quarterback is penciled to start in Los Angeles against the Trojans, but Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith and the other pass-catchers in this room should still perform well and keep the Buckeye offense afloat. The run game will also be watched closely, as more will be expected from this group and it'll get a good test against a strong USC front. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava should make some plays to keep this game competitive, but expect the Ohio State front to stifle an inconsistent rushing attack from the Trojans and force some turnovers to swing the momentum in the Buckeyes’ favor, giving them their 6th straight win and first at USC since 1946. Despite losing star quarterback Julian Sayin for the remainder of the season due to injury, Ohio State remains a 6.5-point road favorite to reign supreme over Lincoln Riley's Trojans. Below, I will break down this Week 9 matchup and provide the betting angles for a same-game parlay that you can take when wagering on Saturday's action! USC vs Ohio State Odds For the first leg of our SGP for Saturday night's conference clash, I feel confident backing Ryan Day's Buckeyes on the moneyline in what could be a closely contested game down the stretch. While the Trojans stock took a major hit this past weekend when Lincoln Riley's bunch got embarrassed by Wisconsin by 17 points in Madison, USC still boasts an elite offense led by quarterback Jayden Maiava — one of the best players in all of college football. Though most were extremely high on Julian Sayin prior to his season-ending injury , I was always under the impression that he was a tad overrated, with a great deal of his success resulting from an elite offensive line and freakish playmaker in wide receiver Jeremiah Smith . While a decision has yet to be made on who will be starting for the Buckeyes under center on Saturday night, we do know that Day will be choosing between Luke Fahey and Tavien St Clair. Both QBs were extremely highly touted coming out of high school, and while it may take some time to adjust to the college game, this is still an Ohio State team that's far superior to USC on both sides of the football. Sure, the Trojans boast an elite offensive unit and now hold a definitive edge at the QB position, but this is a USC program that has dropped the ball in huge games time and again. Despite the uncertainty under center, Ohio State is the far more reliable team of the two, and I would be surprised if it didn't leave the Coliseum with an outright victory on Saturday night. Given Sayin's season-ending injury, we're provided with a rare opportunity to back Ohio State's generational receiver in Jeremiah Smith at a discount — and that's exactly what I'll be buying into. For a program consistently churning out elite receivers, including the likes of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave, Smith still may be the most talented offensive player to ever suit up in Columbus. The junior wideout has already racked up 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns thus far, and I don't expect his elite production to take as big a hit as betting markets appear to suggest. Smith is still the best player in all of college football, and I feel great backing the Buckeyes' phenom to record at least 90 receiving yards on Saturday night at -185. The storylines are vast on both sides, with the main one being injuries on both sides. The Buckeyes are obviously down Julian Sayin on their offense, while the Trojans have a couple of injuries, but none to key contributors on their team. The good news for Ohio State is that while Sayin is out, he doesn't play defense, and Jeremiah Smith is 100 percent ready to go. As long as those two things stay true, the Buckeyes could roll me out at quarterback and have a really good chance to win the football game, especially this one. As it stands right now, the Buckeyes are a one-touchdown favorite against the Trojans by 6.5 points. Nearly the entire public is on the Buckeyes, and for good reason. The performance that USC rolled out last week was a regrettable one for sure. They went all the way across the country to Madison, Wisconsin, to take on the Badgers, and they got an old-school beatdown as a result. From start to finish, the Badgers controlled the physicality of the football game and never allowed the Trojans to get off the mat at all. They forced turnovers, stopped the run, and made USC get into chase mode. They did all of that while registering just 54 passing yards on the game. Ohio State Bye Week: How Are the Buckeyes Going to Approach Life After Julian SayinWe are back on the Buckeye Breakdown Podcast on Ohio State's bye week. No action for the Buckeyes on Saturday, but it was the biggest week of their season as... That could not have happened at a better time for the Buckeyes because it is the exact blueprint that they are going to want to create in this game. The Buckeyes' defense is proving that it is one of the best in the country by far and away. After they figured out some of the negatives in their group against the Illinois Fighting Illini, they have looked totally different. They turned the water off against Iowa, Maryland, and Indiana. They have reverted to their old form, and it is happening at the right time. On offense, they will have their five best offensive lineman up and ready to go today. That group has been a revolving door all year long, but they are the ones that benefited the most from the bye week. They are back to full strength, and the Ohio State rushing attack is going to benefit from that. Finally, No. 4 still plays for the Buckeyes last time that I checked. Anytime you have Jeremiah Smith on your side, you have more than a chance. This is going to be a fast game, one that the Buckeyes choke the clock out, control time of possession, protect their young quarterback, and just try to escape with a win, and I think that they will, easily. The final prediction in this one is Ohio State 24, USC 10. Buckeyes come back home as the No. 2 team in the country with Oregon next up.

One of the more intriguing matchups on the Week 9 college football calendar finds the Buckeyes going on the road against the Trojans without Julian Sayin under center. How does that affect what happens in this battle of college football blue bloods? How Ohio State can win Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown with with wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Regardless of concerns at quarterback, Ohio State has the more complete statistical profile, particularly on defense. The Buckeyes are allowing just 13.4 points and 264.3 total yards per game, ranking fourth and sixth nationally, respectively. Their run defense has been especially effective, giving up only 92.9 rushing yards per game. It should have a decisive edge against a USC ground game that is 105th in FBS and totaling just 131 yards on average. Offensively, Jeremiah Smith has been spectacular yet again. The undefendable wide receiver and Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 52 catches. Even without Sayin, Ohio State can lean on its defense, establish Bo Jackson in the trenches, slow the game down, get the football into Smith's hands, and let him create after the catch. But they're in a very good position to exploit the Buckeyes' uncertainty at quarterback. Applying enough pressure on the edges to rattle Sayin's replacement could give this talented offense enough breathing room to make this interesting. The Trojans are averaging 303.6 passing yards per game, ranking 10th nationally, with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns. USC also converts 50.5 percent of its third downs, the 14th-best rate in the country. That ability to sustain drives could be important against an Ohio State defense that has allowed opponents to convert just 38 percent of third downs. The Trojans need Maiava to protect the football and attack downfield over top OSU's front line defenders. Defensively, USC must pressure the inexperienced Buckeyes quarterback and prevent him from developing any early rhythm. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Make no mistake: the absence of Julian Sayin distributing to the Buckeyes' talented wideouts is a real problem. USC, whatever its defensive lapses in the Riley era, has a legitimate opportunity to make this uncomfortable. Still, Ohio State has a significant defensive advantage overall, allowing just 13 points per game and has an important edge countering the Trojans' ground game that can reduce that offense to one dimension. USC will have opportunities, but Ohio State's defensive consistency ultimately proves to be the edge in the second half. The Big Lead prediction: Ohio State 30, USC 23

The Trojans are coming off a disappointing 24-7 home loss to Wisconsin, and Lincoln Reilly's team is going to have to come up with a much better effort against one of the nation's powerhouse teams. Ohio State is playing its first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin. He suffered an arm injury in Ohio State's 19-15 victory at Indiana earlier in October. Head coach Ryan Day did not name a starter until late Friday when it was revealed that Luke Fahey would be under center instead of Tavien St. Clair. While the Buckeyes have Heisman Trophy favorite Jeremiah Smith at wide receiver and a slew of talented pass catchers, it doesn't seem likely that they will ask Fahey to win the game for them. However, it is clear that the 6.5-point road favorites are asking him not to lose the game. Former USC star Drake London , currently the Atlanta Falcons' top receiver, believes the Trojans have a great chance to come up with the upset. "This is a huge game for USC, and Ohio State has to come all the way across the country and play in SoCal," London told Stephen A. Smith . "My expectation is a W. We are going to play our style of ball. Obviously, Ohio State is Ohio State and they have some dudes, but they don't have a quarterback right now and it's hard to get the ball to No. 4 (Jeremiah Smith) if they don't have a quarterback." Whatever it does should be more than enough to handle a road test at USC on Saturday. That's the opinion of the College Football Power Index. ESPN's algorithmic prediction model sounds very confident in what the Buckeyes can accomplish against the Trojans, even with a new face at the quarterback position. FPI projects Buckeyes will dominate Trojans Oct 17, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) walks off the field with his arm in a sling after the game against the Indiana Hoosiers Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The computer model, which simulates games 20,000 times, projects Ohio State to be 13.4 points better than USC . That's a surprisingly sizable margin for a team heading into a road game without star Julian Sayin. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9 The Buckeyes remain one of college football 's strongest teams, but their quarterback uncertainty makes that projection particularly bold ahead of Saturday's matchup at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Sayin's absence remains the biggest concern after the quarterback suffered a throwing-arm injury during Ohio State's 19-15 victory over Indiana on Oct. 17. Sayin, who threw for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns this season, is expected to be out indefinitely. Who's on deck for the Buckeyes? The uncertainty is compounded by the fact that head coach Ryan Day has not officially named a starter. As of Thursday, both freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair were preparing to play against USC. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions; St. Clair has attempted only seven passes. Neither has demonstrated that he can sustain an offense over a full game against a quality opponent. Trojans can test Ohio State's defense Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) throws against the Northwestern Wildcats during the second half at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images USC also has a capable offense of its own. Quarterback Jayden Maiava has thrown for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns, while the Trojans average 32.8 points per game. Although USC is coming off a 24–7 loss to Wisconsin, its passing game could test Ohio State's defense if the Buckeyes struggle to maintain possession on the other side. The counterargument is Ohio State's defense, which allows just 13.4 points per game, and the presence of star receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. Those strengths help explain why the Buckeyes remain heavily favored by predictive models. Still, a 13-point projection assumes Ohio State can maintain much of its usual efficiency despite a major change at the sport's most important position. Until Fahey or St. Clair proves capable of directing the offense for four quarters, that margin looks ambitious. Ohio State is still the better team, but expecting the Buckeyes to win comfortably in their first game without Sayin is a bold call.

away.headline: What happened to Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin?
away.blurb: “What we're trying to do is give Julian and his family the space and privacy to go through this process,” Day said Oct. 20. “But based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and then also him not being available for the postseason. “If he's not able to return this fall, then we're putting a plan together for that as well. That's the update I have right now." When asked about the possibility of Sayin returning before the end of the regular season, Day said, “I try not to get in any kind of timeline on that. To think that that's going to happen is doubtful.” Sayin has been behind center for the Buckeyes for more than a year, having made 21 consecutive starts since he beat out Lincoln Kienholz in a preseason competition in 2025. Before camp, it was presumed that quarterback Tavien St. Clair would move up after spending last year as the third-stringer. St. Clair stood out during the spring game in April. St. Clair ended as the runner-up for the Mr. Football title, as junior quarterback Matt Ponatoski out of Cincinnati Moeller beat him out by 10 points (70-60). In the fourth quarter of a a 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, Sayin was hurt when he was sacked early in the fourth quarter against the Hoosiers. Defensive lineman Mario Landino collided with Sayin as he began to attempt a pass, causing his arm to bend awkwardly. Sayin had to exit the game early. After leaving for the locker room, he returned with his right throwing arm in a sling. Quarterback Luke Fahey finished the fourth quarter for OSU. home.headline: USC Trojans star JuJu Watkins gets emotional after first game back from injury
home.blurb: JuJu Watkins didn’t hold back her emotions after ending a 588-day absence by making her return from injury in the No. 3 USC Trojans’ 100-68 blowout win over the UNLV Rebels on Monday night. Watkins prepared herself to return in full force, which she successfully pulled off. In 25 minutes of action, she finished with a stat line of 21 points, five rebounds, two assists, and two steals. She shot 9-of-22 from the field and 3-of-4 from the free-throw line. She reflected on her return from injury after the game, expressing immense gratitude that she got to come back to the court with her teammates. “It was great to just be out there with my team again, and to see the first one fall through. It really helped. So yeah, just grateful to be out here today,” Watkins said on the CBS broadcast. “I’m most proud of just my consistency. Like there were days where I could have given up, and so I kept pushing through. And I’m just grateful that I’m here.” JuJu Watkins is on a mission to return to form as one of the best players in the country. She has a promising future ahead of her in the pros, needing to deliver great performances to show she has successfully come back from the severe injury. Related: USC women’s basketball news: Trojans pull off extremely rare feat in JuJu Watkins’ return Watkins started the fourth season of her collegiate career with the Trojans, the third that sees her on the court. She suffered a torn ACL during the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament, an injury that sidelined her for the entire 2025-26 campaign. After dominating Arizona State and looking like the Bears could be a real threat, Baylor suffered back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas, dropping the Bears to 4-3 on the season . The loss to Kansas also ended the Dave Aranda era in Waco. In his seventh season, Aranda was fired and Joe Klanderman will lead the Bears for the remainder of the season as the interim head coach . Klanderman looks to reignite the Baylor Bears and have a strong finish to the season. Baylor will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when the Bears take on UCF . Here's how the staff of Baylor on SI sees the game going. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. UCF has a good offense and Keyone Jenkins has been legit . The Knights just beat BYU and a hangover is certainly possible, but it's not like Baylor has been playing great football. What worries me is the Bears' offensive line. DJ Lagway has been asked to do everything for this offense, and the offensive line can't block for the run game. If Baylor can't run the ball again, it's going to be tough sledding. I look for the home team to make one too many plays. Final score: UCF 27, Baylor 24 Baylor comes off a tough loss to Kansas and has a shorter week facing off against a UCF team that just beat the number 2 ranked team in the country. Should be mostly a passing game given the defenses in this matchup. Baylor has struggled to get the run game going and UCF has had one of the best run defenses in the country right now. Expect a high air-raid offense from both sides, and multiple touchdowns. Baylor will be in their first game without head coach Aranda after getting let go Sunday. My guess is that they will pull one together and slightly outscore this team coming off a big win. The Bears torched UCF in Waco last November 30-3 and will try to rinse and repeat on the road. UCF is undefeated on their home turf and is coming off a dramatic victory over No. 2 BYU, making them 1.5-point favorites over the Bears. Here are three predictions for Joe Klanderman's debut in Baylor's Week 9 matchup: It will still feel like Aranda's team The Bears have parted ways with Dave Aranda after seven years, and Joe Klanderman has stepped into the interim head coach role. Klanderman had just five days to get this team into shape before UCF. While his methods and leadership may be strong, it is surely hard to turn a football team on its head in less than a week. With offensive coordinator Jake Spavital still in charge of the offensive playcalling, I doubt Baylor is going to look dramatically different than they did against Kansas. picks.headline: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF
picks.blurb: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros Week 9 is here and Baylor could look like a different team when it takes the field. The Bears are headed down to Orlando for a Friday night contest against the Knights . UCF is coming off an incredible overtime win over BYU, which gave the Cougars their first loss of the season. As for Baylor, the Bears fired Dave Aranda in his seventh season at the helm. Joe Klanderman has taken over as interim head coach and Baylor's coaching search is underway . Baylor on SI came up with some game props and picked what might happen on Friday night. DJ Lagway throws for O/U 239.5 passing yards IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - OVER Trent Knoop - OVER DJ Lagway has been over this total in two of his last four games, but it does appear that Lagway is getting healthier, which only bodes well for the Bears' offense. UCF doesn't have a great passing defense, and with Baylor struggling to run the ball, Lagway will have to throw to win. Bennett Parker - OVER Personally, I would not touch Lagway O/U lines with a six-foot pole. Through seven games, I still don’t know what to think about his arm talent and decision making. It could very well be another 50% completion, ugly game for Lagway. However, if Baylor plays ‘free’ and ‘energized’ like they have been stressing, Lagway will be at his best and cruise past this line with the help of some trusty receivers and their yards after catch ability. Brad Teague - OVER There is absolutely no reason that DJ Lagway should be under 239 passing yards this week. Yes, Dave Aranda was just fired; but OC Jake Spavital has been calling the offensive plays this season, and is allegedly being now given "the freedom to be as creative as he wants to be" as interim head coach Joe Klanderman said during Media Availability on Monday. He only had 236 yards passing against Kansas last week, but I expect Lagway to excel this week against UCF, playing more freely, and finding numerous receivers on his way to having more than 240 yards passing. I'm taking the OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - OVER I’m leaning toward the over on this one. Even in games where Baylor has struggled offensively, Lagway has found a way to cover this line. I also think Jake Spavital will get creative and find ways to open up the passing game for this offense. Tyler Gillum - OVER UCF’s pass defense has been inconsistent this year averaging just about 240 passing yards per game this year. and Lagway hasn't been under 225 since the Colorado game, coming back from injury. Baylor's defense has O/U 2.5 sacks against UCF IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - UNDER Trent Knoop - UNDER UCF is a top-five team in the Big 12 in sacks allowed. Baylor has an aggressive defense and should get to Keyone Jenkins. But Jenkins is a mobile quarterback who can escape pressure. Scott Frost will dial up some quick passes on Friday in hopes of not allowing Jenkins to stand in the pocket and take heat. The defensive line and linebacker play have been the cornerstone of the Bears’ defense and will continue to be against UCF. Klanderman has sent some well-timed blitzes, and knows how to keep the opposing QB off balance. The Bears had five sacks against Kansas and should at least scare that mark again on Friday. The Bears have the 2nd most sacks in all of the FBS in the first half of games with 17. Baylor has had 3 or more QB sacks in every game except against LA Tech back in September, I don't expect that trend to slow down any time soon. UCF QB Keyone Jenkins, as a playmaker, is going to look to take advantage of Baylor's aggression on the defensive line, but I fully expect Coach Klanderman and the Bears defense to be prepared for exactly that. This game has the potential for a high-count of TFLs, Sks, and FFs . I'm taking an emphatic OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - UNDER Baylor’s defense has been great at generating pressure all season, but I think they’ll finish with two sacks in this matchup. UCF has only allowed more than two sacks in one game this season. The Knights gave up two sacks to both TCU and Houston, along with one sack to BYU and Oklahoma State. Although I’m taking the under, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the Bears come away with three sacks. Tyler Gillum - UNDER Although I do think they can get some pressure on UCF. I think it'll be just about two or maybe even one. Keyone Jenkins showed the ability to escape the pocket and make plays. BYU was able to get just one sack all game with their defense. My prediction is Baylor will likely be the same UCF QB Keyone Jenkins has O/U 250.5 passing yards vs. Baylor Baylor has a good defense, but the Bears have allowed the opposing quarterback to throw for over 251 yards in three of their last four games. Keyone Jenkins has thrown for over 251 yards in his last three outings. The Knights are riding the hot hand and Jenkins' up-tempo style of play can cause some havoc. The Baylor defense has a way of giving up a decent amount of yards without surrendering too many points, allowing 340 per game while averaging just 16.1 points against. The secondary tends to allow some long drives early in the game and the occasional explosive play downfield. I expect UCF to take advantage as much as they can early on. Brad Teague - UNDER He's had some bigger games recently against the 'Pokes (265 yards) and BYU (293 yards), but on the season Keyone Jenkins is only averaging 157 passing yards a game. Not to mention that late in the BYU game, Jenkins would make a visit to the medical tent after being shaken up on a play. There's a chance that his overall drop-backs and longer-developing throws may be limited this week against a Bears defense who will be looking to continue their aggressive gameplay. Provided that Baylor's secondary can limit the penalties being called on them, they're among the top units in all of college football and always hungry for another INT. Keyone Jenkins does not throw for 250 yards in this game; I'm taking the UNDER on this one, Baylor has done a good job of limiting explosive passing plays this season, and I think that trend will continue against UCF. If the Bears can prevent Jenkins from connecting on big plays, I don’t see him surpassing 250 passing yards against this defense. If this game turns into a shootout, he could go over, but I don’t expect that to happen. Although I believe Jenkins will have another solid game, 250 is a lot against this relentless defense. I'm gonna say it'll be just under, but not by much, Jenkins hasn't been under 250 since September against TCU, but the Bears should bring enough pressure for Jenkins to just miss that mark Baylor rushes for O/U 160.5 yards against UCF Until Baylor proves it can run the ball, it's hard to put trust in the run game. It's not due to the running backs themselves. I do think Baylor has a good stable of backs, but the offensive line has been too inconsistent for my liking. This game will come down to DJ Lagway's arm. If Baylor intends on winning this game, they have no choice but to run the ball and run it well. Lagway has shown that he is back to 100% and the O-line is playing with a fire lit under them after struggling in the last couple of games. While I am not convinced by the Bears’ ground game whatsoever, they will get over this total with a lot of help from Lagway. There is zero reason why the Bears shouldn't be able to be well over this mark; except there are, in fact, five reasons why Baylor could miss this target. The Bears offensive line has not had great success this season at fully establishing a solid push and a dominant running game. They're working hard, like to block with and for each other and the Bears team, and seem to be giving it their all; but they've been ineffective throughout most of the season. They've had a 94.5% success rate of keeping the pocket clean on pass plays this season, but have only been able to gain 3.79 rushing yards a carry this season. Currently the Bears are averaging 146.14 rushing yards per game, and unless Dave Aranda getting fired is the catalyst these guys needed to become a stronger unit, I don't see Baylor gaining more than 160 rushing yards; I'm taking the UNDER. Baylor’s running game has been an issue all season, and I don’t expect that to change against the Knights. Against TCU, Baylor averaged just 1.6 yards per carry. Even against Kansas, one of the worst rushing defenses in the conference, the Bears averaged only 3.5 yards per carry, including Lagway’s rushing yards. Based on Baylor’s struggles on the ground this season, I’m taking the under on 160.5 rushing yards. After a rough two weeks of running the ball for Baylor, I don't expect much to change in this one. UCF is coming off a huge win and is ranked 38th in the country in rushing yards allowed on defense. It's going to be a real struggle if the Bears want to move the ball on the ground, and early passing will likely be needed to get any type of momentum on offense. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

Time, Channel, Bold Prediction IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop · Baylor Bears On SI Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The 4-3 Baylor Bears will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when they travel to Orlando to take on the hot UCF Knights . It could be a hangover game for Scott Frost's team , as UCF took down BYU in overtime last week. That was the Cougars' first loss of the season after they upset Notre Dame the week prior. It will also mark the first game without Dave Aranda on the sideline . In his seventh season in Waco, Aranda was fired after the Bears suffered another heartbreaking loss. Rhett Armstrong's kick was blocked last Saturday and the Bears lost to Kansas, giving them two straight losses. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman has assumed the interim head coach job , but will continue to call plays for the defense. It will be interesting to see if Baylor's defense continues to play tough football, or if Klanderman adding another responsibility hits the unit. How to watch Baylor take on UCF IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Day: Friday, Oct. 30 Time: 6:30 p.m. CT Where: Acrisure Bounce House (Orlando, FL) Network: ESPN On the call: Mike Monaco and Jordan Rodgers Radio: Baylor Sports Media Network One bold prediction: Louis Brown goes for 100 yards UCF has allowed 250 or more yards through the air in the last four of five games. If Baylor is going to win this game, the Bears need DJ Lagway to have another big game. Unfortunately, we can't trust the Bears' run game, but that's not because of the running backs. The offensive line has been poor this season, and can't seem to open up many holes for the backs. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has garnered all the attention this season, and for good reason. He is among the top playmakers in the country, averaging nearly 100 yards per game. Freeman has been Lagway's go-to target, and UCF knows that . Freeman will get his targets and yards, but the Bears need to find another target. Louis Brown is Baylor's second-leading wide receiver, catching 22 passes for 345 yards and three touchdowns. He's had a couple of big games. In three games this season, Brown has had five or more catches, along with 62-74 yards. The Knights will try to key in on Freeman, and they won't be able to stop the short passes to Freeman, but if Lagway looks to go deep, Brown could be his man. If Baylor can get another playmaker going alongside Freeman, the Bears have a shot to really get their offense rolling. home.headline: UCF football has QB decision to make, if injuries don't make it first
home.blurb: The team built its offseason around the addition of Alonza Barnett III, a two-year starter at James Madison fresh off Sun Belt Conference Player of the Year honors and a trip to the College Football Playoff. Frost's staff protected its sizable financial investment in Barnett, holding him out of all 15 spring practice sessions as a precaution. Baylor's vaunted defensive front knocked Jenkins out in the third quarter of Friday's 41-9 defeat. Frost said the senior reaggravated an ankle problem, though the severity is unknown. Barnett returned from a five-game absence but could not provide the spark needed to ignite a comeback. UCF flip-flopped through four quarterbacks in 2025, Frost's return to Orlando after seven years - five as Nebraska's head coach. Plans changed two games into the campaign when Barnett sustained a "fairly significant" hamstring injury, sidelining him for more than a month. Keyone Jenkins, a 33-game starter at Florida International, stepped in and steadied the ship at the start of Big 12 play. He led the Knights to their highest-ranked win in program history Oct. 24, a 39-31 double-overtime classic against BYU, with 293 passing yards and four total touchdowns. However, seats could switch again for the stretch run after yet another injury. As November approaches, and with UCF needing another pair of wins to achieve bowl eligibility, uncertainty exists about the starting signal-caller going forward. "I've said a lot that I feel good about our quarterbacks, whoever's in there," Frost said. A familiar problem for UCF head coach Scott Frost Cam Fancher lasted less than a half before getting clobbered on a sack, injuring his back, and then sustained broken ribs at Cincinnati a month later. Tayven Jackson started 10 times, but battled several ailments, including a shoulder joint sprain at Kansas State. Jacurri Brown injured his shoulder in that same game and did not see the field the rest of the year. Fourth-stringer Davi Belfort, now a wide receiver at James Madison, made a few appearances, throwing a game-sealing interception in a loss to Houston. Thus, the root problem lies in the support system, as opposed to strictly a QB's individual performance or toughness. "Whoever was playing quarterback, it's going to be hard if we don't block better and create a running game," Frost said. "I mean, we couldn't get anything going in the first half. We couldn't get a run game going, and we didn't protect very well." Better blocking and rushing production would boost UCF QB Baylor sacked Jenkins, Barnett and true freshman Rocco Marriott a combined seven times. UCF running backs Duke Watson and Landen Chambers gained just 44 yards on 14 attempts. Comparatively, Barnett had the better night in the pocket. He went 8-of-16 passing for 133 yards, finishing with five straight completions. Jenkins was more accurate but settled for shorter throws, finishing 14 of 21 for 82 yards and an interception, a deflection off the hands of receiver Waden Charles

The offense needs to do more to take advantage of the opportunities its defense creates and give that unit some room for error. Baylor enters at 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play after consecutive losses to TCU and Kansas. With five games remaining, the Bears need two more wins to reach bowl eligibility. Defense Looks to Finish Stronger After Kansas Loss Even without them, Baylor’s defense has generally done enough to give the Bears a chance to win. The unit held each of its first six opponents to 20 points or fewer before allowing 25 at Kansas. Finishing games will be a priority for Klanderman as he takes over. Baylor has shown it can pressure quarterbacks and force turnovers, but it needs to pair those disruptive plays with more consistent stops late in games. home.headline: UCF football trounced by Baylor in Space Game; Alonza Barnett III returns
home.blurb: Alonza Barnett III makes UCF return Barnett, however, could not provide an immediate spark. UCF went three-and-out as he was sacked on second down by a blitzing Bo Onu. UCF went three-and-out on its two-minute drill, allowing Baylor an opportunity to go ahead 20-3 with 28 seconds left in the half. Rhett Armstrong made a 29-yard field goal, his second in as many possessions for the Bears. Keyone Jenkins' second pass of the night bounced off the hands of UCF receiver Waden Charles and into the waiting arms of Baylor cornerback Devon Jordan. The Bears take over at UCF's 46-yard line following a penalty during the return. DJ Lagway picked up one first down with his legs, but took an intentional grounding to force a punt on Baylor's opening drive. Palmer Williams skied a 50-yard kick, plus a holding penalty on the return, to pin the Knights deep in their own end. UCF went three-and-out, gaining just one yard on their three plays against the Bears' stingy defense. UCF QB Alonza Barnett III could be available Keyone Jenkins will make his sixth straight start at quarterback for UCF, but Alonza Barnett III could be available for the Knights if needed. For the second week in a row, Barnett is considered a game-time decision on the Big 12's final availability report. Coach Scott Frost said he will ride the "hot hand" and keep Keyone Jenkins at quarterback for tonight's game against Baylor. Alonza Barnett III is still not 100% after suffering a hamstring injury Sept. 12 at Pitt. The James Madison transfer was available in an emergency capacity for last week's game against BYU. home.headline: Kansas HC Lance Leipold Remains Noncommittal on Isaiah Marshall's Status vs. UCF
home.blurb: Many Kansas football fans are checked out with the state of the program after another grueling loss last week to TCU. However, the Jayhawks still have one-third of the campaign to go sitting at 3-5. In KU's most recent defeat, quarterback Isaiah Marshall was inactive for the first time this year due to a lower-leg injury. In his place, backup Cole Ballard returned to action after dealing with a shoulder ailment of his own. For the Jayhawks to realistically stay in the race for bowl eligibility this Saturday against UCF, they very much need Marshall to return under center. However, it remains far from a sure thing that the redshirt sophomore makes his way back to the field over the weekend. Head coach Lance Leipold remained noncommittal on his quarterback choice during his weekly press conference today. Marshall has been banged up since the start of the year, which isn't surprising given his lean frame and how involved he is in the rushing attack. Still, there was no indication that his status for the TCU contest was in jeopardy until he popped up on the injury report three days before kickoff. He was then downgraded to questionable and ultimately was held out for precautionary reasons as a game-time decision.
